Skip types\\n   already covered by unchanged existing artifacts.\\n5. Run the artifact preview command. Inspect its type, destination path, and\\n   `allocated_id`.\\n6. Repeat actions 4\\u20139 for each remaining missing definition.\\n\\n| Order | Artifact | TYPE | Content | Declared links |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| 1 | Intent (INT) | `intent` | Problem, intended outcome, affected users, and scope limits. | None required here. |\\n| 2 | Capability (CAP) | `capability` | The ability needed to achieve the outcome. | `derives_from` \\u2192 intent (INT). |\\n| 3 | Requirement (REQ) | `requirement` | Observable behavior, conditions, and acceptance criteria. | `derives_from` \\u2192 capability (CAP). |\\n| 4 | Specification (SPEC) | `specification` | Detailed behavior, constraints, failure behavior, and checkable examples. | `specifies` \\u2192 requirement (REQ). |\\n| 5 | Architecture (ARCH), when applicable | `architecture` | Components, boundaries, and the architecture decision assessment. | `addresses` \\u2192 requirement (REQ); `conforms_to` \\u2192 specification (SPEC). |\\n| 6 | Architecture decision (ADR), when required | `adr` | Context, alternatives, chosen design, and consequences. | `decides` \\u2192 architecture (ARCH). |\\n\\nRecord an unresolved design choice for [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec). Do not present a recommendation\\nas an agreed architecture decision (ADR). Prepare verification contracts (VER)\\nin [Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified).\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor a missing domain, use the first command in action 2 and the second only\\nafter reviewing the preview in action 3:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl scaffold-domain REPO --domain DOMAIN --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl scaffold-domain REPO --domain DOMAIN --json\\n```\\n\\nFor each missing artifact, use this **creation sequence** in actions 5\\u20136.\\nReplace `TYPE` with the table value. Replace `ARTIFACT-ID` in the second\\ncommand with the first command's `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --id ARTIFACT-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nThe preview writes nothing and does not reserve an ID. Their acceptance\\nis handled in the authorization process.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c38865671a81429dd291d9f9bb333deae02a4098d4afcf034f293ee919e990e0\"}, {\"heading\": \"define-how-the-result-will-be-verified\", \"title\": \"Define how the result will be verified\", \"anchor\": \"define-how-the-result-will-be-verified\", \"start_line\": 109, \"end_line\": 165, \"content\": \"### Define how the result will be verified\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected requirements (REQ), specifications (SPEC), proposed\\namendments, and existing verification contracts (VER).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New or updated verification contracts (VER) in\\n  `draft` where coverage is missing. None created or modified where existing\\n  contracts provide unchanged coverage. Accepted contracts remain unchanged.\\n- **Transient working material:** The selection of reused verification\\n  contracts (VER), any amendment proposals prepared through [Propose any needed amendments to existing definitions](AMEND_DEFINITIONS.md#propose-any-needed-amendments-to-existing-definitions), coverage\\n  gaps, and unresolved questions. Retain these under the same conditions\\n  as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Read each selected requirement's (REQ) acceptance criteria and linked\\n   specifications (SPEC).\\n2. Compare those criteria with the existing verification contracts (VER).\\n3. Select unchanged contracts that cover the proposed behavior.\\n4. For each coverage gap, create a verification contract (VER) with the\\n   commands below, or use [Propose any needed amendments to existing definitions](AMEND_DEFINITIONS.md#propose-any-needed-amendments-to-existing-definitions) to propose an amendment to an existing one.\\n5. Complete `Requirement-to-evidence matrix`. For each requirement (REQ),\\n   record its ID, method, case or evidence, and pass condition. Use `test`,\\n   `analysis`, `inspection`, or `demonstration` as the method.\\n6. Specify the inputs, platform, evaluator, and command or manual actions for\\n   each check. Derive expected results from the requirement (REQ) and\\n   specification (SPEC), not from candidate output.\\n7. Set `[relations].verifies` to the covered requirement (REQ) IDs.\\n8. Complete `Independence`, `Evidence retention`, and applicable assessment\\n   sections in each new or edited draft.\\n9. Apply `## verification` \\u2192 `### Checklist` in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n10. Retain questions about missing criteria or methods for [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec).\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor each new verification contract (VER), run the creation sequence from\\n[Draft any missing definitions](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#draft-any-missing-definitions) with these arguments. Inspect the preview before creation; replace\\n`VER-ID` with its `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type verification --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type verification --id VER-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nNo harness command writes the verification method or pass criteria. The human\\nor agent completes that content. No verification record (VREC) is created here.\\n\\n**Completion:** Every selected requirement (REQ) has a defined verification\\nmethod and pass condition, or an explicit unresolved question. Each proposed\\ncheck identifies how to perform it and where its evidence will be retained.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements) links these contracts to work orders (WO). The execution\\nand verification processes later perform the checks and assess the evidence.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"16a9ea7323450e244b26edd2d1ad757048124b627bcfffa157c8b173f57f363c\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract\", \"title\": \"Prepare a release or operating contract\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract\", \"start_line\": 166, \"end_line\": 220, \"content\": \"### Prepare a release or operating contract\\n\\n**Inputs:** A proposed release or ongoing operating obligation, its scope,\\nexisting work-order or requirement IDs, and any accepted contract that may\\nalready cover it.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** A completed release-contract (REL) or operating-contract\\n  (OPS) draft when needed. An accepted contract is reused only if its meaning\\n  and scope already cover the proposed obligation.\\n- **Transient working material:** Selection notes, new IDs and paths, and\\n  unresolved questions. No release or operating authorization is inferred.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Decide which obligation applies: release scope uses `release_contract`;\\n   continuing assurance uses `operating_contract`. Do not create both by default.\\n2. Read existing contracts selected for reuse. If an accepted contract needs\\n   changed meaning, use the accepted-definition amendment boundary; do not edit\\n   it through this draft-creation procedure.\\n3. For a missing contract, use the supported domain and artifact creation\\n   sequence from \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Inspect the dry-run result and use its\\n   returned `allocated_id` in the creation command.\\n4. Complete the generated body and accountable metadata. For a REL, record\\n   release scope, version conditions, rollback, and evidence expectations.\\n   For an OPS, record measurable observability, support, and operating obligations.\\n5. Set `REL.gates` to every existing work-order ID covered by the release\\n   contract, or `OPS.assures` to every existing requirement ID for which it\\n   claims continuing assurance. Do not leave invented or unresolved IDs.\\n6. Apply `## release_contract` or `## operating_contract` and its `### Checklist`\\n   in `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n7. Validate the completed draft and resolve findings within the proposed scope.\\n8. Include the contract in [Authorize the work](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#procedure) for the exact human decision.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nHere `TYPE` is `release_contract` or `operating_contract`, selected in action 1:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --id CONTRACT-ID --json\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\n**Completion:** The applicable contract is covered by an unchanged accepted\\nrecord or a completed draft ready for its decision. Unresolved amendments\\nremain visible and block dependent work.\\n\\n**Later use:** An accepted REL governs release preparation. An accepted OPS\\ngoverns its stated continuing obligations after delivery. Perform the checks\\nand follow-up actions named in the OPS at its specified triggers; one successful\\ndelivery does not establish continuing conformance. External operating actions\\nstill require their exact authority.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"723a469b890666ae4b1e7b95a6231200a6794e6b792fef8e043ed82bc4f96ce5\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-final40-20261012\\\\claude-361\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"design-simplicity\", \"title\": \"Design simplicity\", \"anchor\": \"design-simplicity\", \"start_line\": 21, \"end_line\": 58, \"content\": \"## Design simplicity\\n\\nFor unfinished work, `harnessctl validate-draft REPO --artifact ID --json`\\nreports whether one supported draft has an admissible shape. Only exact values\\nat the same type and field in this evaluator's canonical template, and missing\\nor empty required authoring links, can be reported as incomplete. Invalid\\nidentity, dates, metadata shapes, actual endpoints, lifecycle history and\\ndisposition are errors. A missing non-template ID is an error. Background\\nfindings remain visible; this result makes no whole-repository validity claim.\\nComplete the authoring checklist and pass ordinary approval gates before\\nrequesting approval. Draft admission grants no authority to write or approve.\\n\\nChoose the least complex design that satisfies the agreed requirements and\\nconstraints. Justify material added complexity by the need it serves and why\\na simpler approach is insufficient. Consider the effort to understand, build,\\ntest, operate and change the whole solution. Defer speculative needs. Review\\nboth the necessity of the specified behavior and the simplicity of its\\nimplementation. Preserve correctness and the project's required quality and\\nsafety properties.\\n\\nStart from the smallest complete solution. Each project supplies its agreed\\nusers, scale, operating conditions and quality constraints. Agreed future needs\\ncan matter; imagined flexibility alone is insufficient. Credible risk analysis\\ncan justify prevention before an incident. Fewer lines, shorter specifications\\nor fewer tests do not establish simplicity; moving work to users, operations\\nor dependencies also has a cost.\\n\\nApply the relevant questions below before definition approval and during design\\nand implementation review. Return unjustified obligations or design complexity\\nfor revision through the existing decision process. Explain material choices\\nin the existing specification, design or review: the need, why a simpler option\\nis insufficient and the added cost. Scale the explanation to the decision; a\\nsmall choice may need one sentence, a significant design may use its existing\\narchitecture decision. Trivial changes need no separate comparison document.\\n\\nThese are human review standards. They introduce no separate KISS artifact,\\nmandatory score, receipt, automated simplicity gate or additional approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"29e9b6296f39215c4b2ad36659c0674f0b20650682db9aa1187fc97871cfdb06\"}, {\"heading\": \"intent\", \"title\": \"intent\", \"anchor\": \"intent\", \"start_line\": 76, \"end_line\": 84, \"content\": \"## intent\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Explain the present problem, who it affects, and the outcome wanted.\\n- What is the smallest useful outcome, and which needs and constraints are actually agreed?\\n- Say how the owner will know the change helped; an honest baseline may be `not measured`.\\n- State the important scope limits. Create a new intent when the desired outcome changes.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"291e8274f0c400a3d2d1ecdd56f2c10d68ab6cb40f667076a034e44d87c05e42\"}]}]}",

Scoring and categories are optional.                                                                                          | A concern needs follow-up. A separate decision (DEC) is used when the concern must block work.                                                           |\\n| `operating_contract`  | `OPS-`    | Defines continuing service, support, monitoring, or operational assurance obligations.                                                                                       | Ongoing operational commitments apply. Omitting the record does not prove those commitments have been met.                                               |\\n\\nCode, tests, acceptance scenarios, evidence files, commits, dashboards, tickets,\\nand conversations are not additional formal artifact types. They may support\\nor be referenced by formal artifacts but do not grant authority by themselves.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"47268c9ec1e3551fb547ad3d1ef7b8da0b773b52b3a4364f42c36cc64f98bf83\"}, {\"heading\": \"artifact-locations\", \"title\": \"Artifact locations\", \"anchor\": \"artifact-locations\", \"start_line\": 63, \"end_line\": 96, \"content\": \"## Artifact locations\\n\\nNew formal artifacts use these directories below\\n`docs/engineering/DOMAIN/`. `DOMAIN` is the selected domain name. These paths\\ndescribe storage, not authority; the artifact ID, metadata, and typed links\\nremain authoritative. Use the supported authoring command to obtain the actual\\npath. Do not move existing records merely to match this table.\\n\\n| Artifact | TYPE | Directory |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Intent (INT) | `intent` | `intent/` |\\n| Capability (CAP) | `capability` | `capabilities/` |\\n| Requirement (REQ) | `requirement` | `requirements/` |\\n| Specification (SPEC) | `specification` | `specifications/` |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) | `architecture` | `architecture/` |\\n| Architecture decision (ADR) | `adr` | `architecture/adr/` |\\n| Verification contract (VER) | `verification` | `verification/` |\\n| Work order (WO) | `work_order` | `work-orders/` |\\n| Verification record (VREC) | `verification_record` | `verification-records/` |\\n| Release contract (REL) | `release_contract` | `release/` |\\n| Release record (RLS) | `release_record` | `releases/` |\\n| Operating contract (OPS) | `operating_contract` | `operations/` |\\n| Decision (DEC) | `decision` | `decisions/` |\\n| Risk (RISK) | `risk` | `risks/` |\\n\\nThe same domain has `evidence/` for retained work-order evidence and\\n`acceptance/` for acceptance scenarios. These are supporting files, not new\\nformal artifact types. Legacy flat artifact locations remain readable and\\nMUST NOT be moved by an upgrade without separate authority.\\n\\nTemplates under `docs/engineering/templates/` are authoring assets. They are\\nexcluded from active-artifact validation and grant no authority. Use\\n`capture-verification` and `prepare-release` for commit-bound VREC and RLS\\ninstances; an edited template is not a substitute for their derived evidence.\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8df276d2f837c4dcc663dbdb42c67cbb6f8fe3bf4abcb53acf86bc7538269a72\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DEFINITION_LINKS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-final40-20261012\\\\claude-361\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DEFINITION_LINKS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"75b0c06f90fbb219fc31684a1a2d97987215dbada20e335656e45a57532c3010\", \"bytes\": 3505, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"links-between-definitions\", \"title\": \"Links between definitions\", \"anchor\": \"links-between-definitions\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 35, \"content\": \"## Links between definitions\\n\\nAn arrow points from the artifact that records the link to the artifact it\\nreferences. These links describe meaning and coverage, not execution order.\\n\\nRepository validation, draft validation and work-order preflight share the\\ndeclared source/relation/target types. A supplied undeclared relation or a target\\nof the wrong type is invalid even when no work order selects the artifact.\\nPreflight still evaluates readiness only for its selected governing chain.\\nThe read-only draft query permits specific unfinished authoring slots; ordinary\\nvalidation and approval retain their completeness requirements.\\n\\n```mermaid\\nflowchart LR\\n    CAP[\\\"Capability (CAP)\\\"] -->|derives_from| INT[\\\"Intent (INT)\\\"]\\n    REQ[\\\"Requirement (REQ)\\\"] -->|derives_from| CAP\\n    SPEC[\\\"Specification (SPEC)\\\"] -->|specifies| REQ\\n    VER[\\\"Verification contract (VER)\\\"] -->|verifies| REQ\\n    ARCH[\\\"Architecture (ARCH)\\\"] -->|addresses| REQ\\n    ARCH -->|conforms_to| SPEC\\n    ADR[\\\"Architecture decision (ADR)\\\"] -->|decides| ARCH\\n```\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Capability (CAP) \\u2192 Intent (INT) | `derives_from` | Each active capability (CAP) names one or more active intents (INT). |\\n| Requirement (REQ) \\u2192 Capability (CAP) | `derives_from` | Each active requirement (REQ) names one or more active capabilities (CAP). |\\n| Specification (SPEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `specifies` | Each requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO) needs one or more selected active specifications (SPEC). |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `addresses` | The architecture (ARCH) names every requirement (REQ) that materially drives its structure. |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) \\u2192 Specification (SPEC) | `conforms_to` | For each addressed requirement (REQ), the selected architecture (ARCH) names at least one selected specification (SPEC) covering it. |\\n| Architecture decision (ADR) \\u2192 Architecture (ARCH) | `decides` | Each selected architecture (ARCH) that requires a design decision has at least one selected active architecture decision (ADR). |\\n| Verification contract (VER) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `verifies` | Each selected requirement (REQ) has one or more selected active verification contracts (VER). |\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"7e7361437700c3a1bf7d9add02accf3a4d3ee3fa48dbdc0ba0b991b40514071a\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DEFINE_CHANGE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-final40-20261012\\\\claude-361\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DEFINE_CHANGE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"7f41ea6b62df110755524d88293019406d6cf6a238abc67e795db98234024f52\", \"bytes\": 10552, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nA new change needs an outcome, limits or selection of existing artifacts.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c2cb6d6aa5d04e2579b2641ce2d738fd1359afb9a7b30a63652e4dfa3b8db8d9\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore selecting artifacts, read [ARTIFACTS.md#artifact-types](ARTIFACTS.md#artifact-types) and [DEFINITION_LINKS.md#links-between-definitions](DEFINITION_LINKS.md#links-between-definitions).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"3ce477685d52f9c993e2006dcb2e0e67c0beb152b3570f7b808f5af8367ec631\"}, {\"heading\": \"identify-the-existing-artifacts-that-apply-to-the-change\", \"title\": \"Identify the existing artifacts that apply to the change\", \"anchor\": \"identify-the-existing-artifacts-that-apply-to-the-change\", \"start_line\": 110, \"end_line\": 177, \"content\": \"### Identify the existing artifacts that apply to the change\\n\\n**Inputs:** The confirmed outcome, scope limits, any artifact IDs supplied\\nin the request, and the existing formal records. Use\\n`docs/engineering/README.md` when locating a domain.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None created or modified.\\n- **Transient working material:** A list of selected artifacts (the artifact\\n  inventory), a list of missing definitions, and the evaluator results.\\n  These are needed only for the current change-definition context. The agent\\n  SHALL retain them in the conversation or, at its discretion, in a temporary\\n  location outside the repository. They SHALL NOT be persisted in the\\n  repository. The agent chooses whether a temporary file is needed and, if\\n  so, its filename and format.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Run the repository inspection command below.\\n2. If the request selects a work order (WO), run the selected-work command\\n   below. Read that work order (WO) and every file in the returned\\n   `context.reading_manifest`.\\n3. Otherwise, locate the artifacts named in the request. If none are named,\\n   use `docs/engineering/README.md` to locate the domain covering the function\\n   or component in the scope. Read its intents (INT), capabilities (CAP),\\n   and requirements (REQ). Record a missing domain if none covers the change.\\n4. Select the requirements (REQ) whose behavior the change would modify or\\n   reuse. Trace each one back to its capabilities (CAP) and intents (INT).\\n5. Read the specifications (SPEC), applicable architectures (ARCH), architecture\\n   decisions (ADR), verification contracts (VER), and work orders (WO) linked\\n   to those selected requirements (REQ). Use the declared relations listed\\n   in [Definition links](DEFINITION_LINKS.md#links-between-definitions). Keep unrelated work outside the selected scope.\\n6. Read decisions (DEC) and risks (RISK) that name the selected artifacts.\\n7. For each selected artifact, retain its name and code, such as Requirement\\n   (REQ), its ID, file path, current lifecycle state, and why it applies to the\\n   change. Keep this list as transient working material; do not create a\\n   repository inventory file.\\n8. Assign one treatment to each entry: `reuse`, `amend`, or `reference only`.\\n   Use `reuse` only when its existing meaning covers the change unchanged.\\n9. List missing definitions by type and purpose. Identify their intended domain.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nRepository inspection, used in action 1:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl inspect REPO --json\\n```\\n\\nSelected-work inspection, used in action 2. Replace `WO-ID` with the actual\\nwork order (WO) ID:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nBoth commands are read-only. `inspect` does not select the change scope.\\nThe checkpoint-free `check` reports lifecycle context without evaluating\\ncheckpoint gates. Preserve its reported blockers and next action.\\n\\n**Completion:** One inventory identifies the existing artifacts to reuse,\\namend, or consult and the definitions that are missing. Ambiguous artifact\\nidentities are resolved before dependent drafting.\\n\\n**Later use:** The inventory controls creation in [Draft any missing definitions](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#draft-any-missing-definitions), amendments in [Propose any needed amendments to existing definitions](AMEND_DEFINITIONS.md#propose-any-needed-amendments-to-existing-definitions),\\nand the verification, risk, decision, and work-order work in [Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified), [Record risks (RISK) affecting the change](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change), [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec), [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"7b2f2d344ca3f55a24c469e2da9819fe937be5467541f815a2f53d2316b7c8b8\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-final40-20261012\\\\claude-361\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"c4ffde0efff3a57df41cf6b282896e6827ea289607f8b73faa8f7c09d0c70213\", \"bytes\": 8654, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nDefinitions, work scope and verification requirements are ready for work planning.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"3977586afdaba8e900cfd38bfd72b02ccf3d011048dae4b247fe81a24c64c9cc\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nRead [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#links-from-work-orders-wo](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#links-from-work-orders-wo), [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope) and [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). Apply [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity) and [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#work_order](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#work_order).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d2a9a7707114a465ebde20884e2a996807663ab4aa94ff11008f2360617efe50\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements\", \"title\": \"Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 143, \"content\": \"### Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements\\n\\n**Inputs:** The outcome, scope, artifact inventory, definition drafts,\\namendment proposals, verification contracts (VER), risks (RISK), and\\nunresolved decisions (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New or completed work orders (WO) in `draft`.\\n  Applicable risks (RISK) and open decisions (DEC) updated with the actual\\n  work order (WO) links. Lifecycle states and dispositions are preserved.\\n  Approved work orders (WO) remain unchanged; proposed scope changes require\\n  review.\\n- **Transient working material:** The review handoff and evaluator results.\\n  Retain these under the same conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Inspect the implementation and follow its callers, references and consumers.\\n   Check tests and fixtures, instructions and documentation, packaging and CI,\\n   and verification outputs where they apply. Keep the working inventory in\\n   the conversation or temporary storage outside the repository.\\n   Group each complete, independently verifiable outcome into one bounded\\n   work order with its necessary supporting changes.\\n2. Select an existing work order (WO) in `draft` for a unit only if its scope\\n   matches. Otherwise, create a new work order (WO) with the commands below.\\n3. Complete each draft using the field table below. In Expected change\\n   surface, name the inspected paths and give a short reason for each.\\n   Explain non-applicable areas and unknown destinations briefly.\\n4. Check that every selected requirement (REQ) has the specification (SPEC)\\n   and verification contract (VER) coverage defined in [Complete work scope](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope).\\n5. Apply `## work_order` \\u2192 `### Checklist` in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n6. Add the new work order (WO) IDs to applicable `threatens` relations in risks\\n   (RISK) and `concerns` or `blocks` relations in open decisions (DEC). Keep\\n   every blocked ID in `concerns`. Preserve any required pairing between the\\n   risk (RISK) and decision (DEC).\\n7. If the planned change needs a missing release or operating contract,\\n   use [Prepare a release or operating contract](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract) now that the work\\n   order IDs exist. Include its draft in the proposed package.\\n8. Run the validation command below.\\n9. Correct findings within the proposed drafts. Rerun validation after edits.\\n   Report unrelated findings separately. Retain findings that need a decision\\n   or an accepted-definition amendment as unresolved dependencies.\\n10. Run the selected-work check below for each proposed work order (WO).\\n    Supply every planned file from Expected change surface with\\n    `--planned-path`. Inspect `scope.preparation`: resolve uncovered or\\n    invalid paths in the draft before requesting approval. A successful\\n    command exit does not establish coverage or a complete impact analysis.\\n    Explain future generated destinations using\\n    [Generated outputs](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#generated-outputs).\\n11. Present the outcome, scope, artifact IDs and paths, validation results,\\n    unresolved decisions (DEC), and unapplied amendments. Include the\\n    evaluator's reported next action for each selected work order (WO).\\n\\n| Field or section | Content |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `Objective` | The outcome this work order (WO) will deliver. |\\n| `In scope` / `Out of scope` | The boundaries from [Define the limits of the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#define-the-limits-of-the-change) assigned to this work order (WO). |\\n| `Constraints` | The conditions from [Define the limits of the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#define-the-limits-of-the-change) that apply to this work. |\\n| `Expected change surface` | Inspected planned paths, the reason for each, and unresolved destinations. |\\n| `[execution_scope].paths` | Exact repository-relative files or component directories ending in `/`. Use forward slashes; no wildcards, absolute paths, or `..`. |\\n| `Authorized decision envelope` | What the implementer may decide and what requires another accountable decision. |\\n| `Required verification` / `Evidence to record` | The checks and retained outputs defined in [Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified). |\\n| `Stop and escalate conditions` | The conditions that require pausing this work. |\\n| `Completion report format` | The required report of completed behavior, checks, limitations, and next accountable decision. |\\n| `[assurance]` | `commit_bound_verification`, its `rationale`, and `decided_by`. Apply the classification rules in [Assurance classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). Record the human who confirmed the classification; an agent may propose it and record that human's decision. |\\n| `[relations]` | `implements` \\u2192 requirements (REQ); `specifications` \\u2192 specifications (SPEC); `verification` \\u2192 verification contracts (VER); `architecture` \\u2192 applicable architectures (ARCH) and required architecture decisions (ADR). |\\n\\nFor PR-based work, include the proposed [review-publication grant](AUTHORITY.md#review-publication-authority)\\nin the decision envelope. Name its repository, source branch, target branch\\nand selected work. Include both the ready-record publication and the later\\ndecision-only push in the expected scope. Present that grant explicitly with\\nimplementation approval; do not infer it from ordinary work authority.\\n\\nIf the assurance classification has not been confirmed, present it as a\\nproposal in the review handoff. Report the missing decision. Do not fill\\n`decided_by` with the draft author's name or an example identity to satisfy\\nvalidation. The human may confirm the classification while reviewing the\\nwork order; record that decision before previewing approval.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor each new work order (WO), run the creation sequence from [Draft any missing definitions](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#draft-any-missing-definitions).\\nInspect the preview before creation; replace `WO-ID` with its `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type work_order --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type work_order --id WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nValidate the formal artifacts after completing the drafts and links:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\nInspect each proposed work order (WO) using its actual ID:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nTo assess the proposed file list, repeat `--planned-path` for every file:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --planned-path PATH --planned-path ANOTHER-PATH --json\\n```\\n\\nThis option is available only when the selected released evaluator supports\\nit. If it is unavailable, report that version gap; do not run candidate\\nsource to govern the repository.\\n\\nThe optional planning view evaluates no checkpoint. It reports explicit\\nscope matches, existing automatic admission, uncovered paths and invalid\\ndeclarations. It does not inspect dependencies for the agent, prove that\\nthe supplied list is complete, or turn planned paths into observed changes.\\nDo not combine it with checkpoint or actual-change inputs.\\n\\nValidation does not approve the change. The checkpoint-free `check` reports\\nlifecycle context without evaluating checkpoint gates.\\n\\n**Completion:** Draft work orders (WO) are presented for review with their\\ngoverning artifacts and evaluator results. Every unresolved dependency is\\nidentified. Preparation does not approve or start execution.\\n\\n**Later use:** The authorization process reviews this artifact package,\\nresolves approval blockers, and applies permitted lifecycle transitions.\\nOnly the formal artifacts carry lasting definitions and work authority;\\ntransient working material is not persisted in the repository.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ee93a263dcebc650ee59519ecaafa4c005120db60b83b8acc6bf4191efe3c8dd\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-final40-20261012\\\\claude-361\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"capability\", \"title\": \"capability\", \"anchor\": \"capability\", \"start_line\": 85, \"end_line\": 93, \"content\": \"## capability\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Say what an actor should be able to do and any relevant conditions.\\n- Does each supported case serve an agreed need under those conditions?\\n- Link the intent it serves. The graph lists the derived requirements.\\n- Put implementation details where they help the implementer; no required `can ... under` wording.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ee6452eeeb618cbe10c941638e7f6be38d2709f53e169920c2d3d012c94ce978\"}, {\"heading\": \"requirement\", \"title\": \"requirement\", \"anchor\": \"requirement\", \"start_line\": 59, \"end_line\": 75, \"content\": \"## requirement\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- State the observable behavior and why it is needed. Ordinary language is accepted; `SHALL` is optional.\\n- What agreed outcome does this obligation serve, for whom and under which conditions? Separate requirements from assumptions and speculative needs.\\n- Include a concrete acceptance condition in `Examples`, `Acceptance`, `measure`, `verification_notes`, or a linked verification contract.\\n- Name the source capability and a verification method. Supported method arrays contain `test`, `analysis`, `inspection`, or `demonstration`; retained text methods remain readable.\\n- Replace unfinished placeholders and resolve blocking decisions before approval.\\n\\n### Guidance\\n\\nWrite enough for someone to implement and check the behavior. Use the template's\\nsections when helpful. Word counts, sentence shapes and numbers of code references\\nare not checked. Writing hints never block approval. Optional metadata must still\\nhave a valid value when supplied.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"333872b200842af881c6c22cfcb0631897071421f423885b2702ac6b72c75770\"}, {\"heading\": \"specification\", \"title\": \"specification\", \"anchor\": \"specification\", \"start_line\": 94, \"end_line\": 107, \"content\": \"## specification\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Explain what an implementation must do, including meaningful failure behavior.\\n- Is each promised behavior necessary? Could a simpler contract meet the agreed need? Prescribe a mechanism only when it is a necessary constraint.\\n- Link the requirements and show an example someone can check.\\n- Give a rule a stable identifier when evidence or a decision needs to refer to it.\\n- Check that supplied rule references exist and identifiers are unambiguous.\\n\\nMissing summaries and ambiguous rule references may produce draft hints. Hints\\nhelp a reviewer; they do not withhold approval. Existing approved text need not\\nbe rewritten to adopt these checklists.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"7aeefa5f4ed363ecdef5185d2b776c6fdd9146ece8e2bfd7ae1ee852f0acf6e1\"}, {\"heading\": \"verification\", \"title\": \"verification\", \"anchor\": \"verification\", \"start_line\": 126, \"end_line\": 135, \"content\": \"## verification\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Independence: expected values derive from the requirements and specifications, never from candidate output.\\n- A requirement-to-evidence matrix with a pass condition per requirement.\\n- Cover normal behavior and meaningful failure outcomes or risks; do not invent failure scenarios to fill a template.\\n- What accepted behavior or quality does each test or CI check establish? Cover distinct relevant outcomes, reuse applicable evidence, and avoid mirroring every implementation branch or combination.\\n- Pass criteria name the platforms and the evaluator.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e6d36e5fe7a23845861e67079317f856b4f892d7f17c4f3d4dbdb4476edb7720\"}, {\"heading\": \"work_order\", \"title\": \"work_order\", \"anchor\": \"work_order\", \"start_line\": 136, \"end_line\": 146, \"content\": \"## work_order\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `[execution_scope].paths` is exact: files or component-prefix directories, nothing wider.\\n- `[assurance]` is classified and its rationale names what later decisions depend on.\\n- In scope and out of scope are both stated; the decision envelope says what the implementer may and may not decide.\\n- Stop conditions and the completion report format are stated.\\n- Is every planned change needed for the agreed outcome? Include removal or adjustment of obsolete behavior, tests and instructions within the approved scope.\\n- Inspect supporting paths before approval and assess the supplied plan through [Draft work orders](harness/DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements). These commands do not\n128\tapprove work, accept verification, or release artifacts.\n129\t\n130\t## Repository setup and inspection\n131\t\n132\t```text\n133\tharnessctl init [TARGET] [--project-name NAME] [--integration git|ci|pr] [--dry-run] [--json]\n134\tharnessctl validate [TARGET] [--json] [--advisories]\n135\tharnessctl inspect [TARGET] [--json] [--vocabulary-threshold N]\n136\tharnessctl dashboard [TARGET] [--output PATH] [--json]\n137\tharnessctl doctor [TARGET] [--json]\n138\t```\n139\t\n140\t`TARGET` defaults to the current directory. A body uses either\n236\t`Harness-Work-Order: WO-AAA-001` or\n237\t`Harness-Work-Orders: WO-AAA-001, WO-BBB-002`. Use `--field work-orders`\n238\tfor one ID per output line. LF and CRLF are equivalent. Both declarations\n239\ttogether, duplicate IDs and malformed IDs are rejected.\n240\t\n241\t```sh\n242\tharnessctl check-pr [TARGET] --event EVENT.json --from-git BASE [--json]\n243\t```\n244\t\n245\t`check-pr` evaluates every selected approved work order and the complete diff\n246\tagainst their combined scope. Unrelated changes are not admitted by listing\n247\tanother work order; that work order must actually cover the path. In-progress\n248\twork also needs passing local handoff checks. CI calls this command directly.\n249\t\n250\t\n251\t## Selected-scope workflow execution\n252\t\n253\tThe command shapes below are stable interfaces. The candidate standard\n254\t[`CONTINUE.md`](../../templates/repository/standard/docs/engineering/harness/CONTINUE.md#continue-selected-work)\n255\troutes to the selected procedure, and\n256\t[`WORKFLOW.json`](../../templates/repository/standard/docs/engineering/WORKFLOW.json)\n257\tis the machine-readable contract loaded by `harnessctl`. Use the workflow rule\n258\tselected for the artifact's exact type, state, and direct related records. Do\n259\tnot derive a new transition or next action from this reference.\n260\t\n261\t```text\n262\tharnessctl evidence [TARGET] --artifact WO-... --checkpoint start|pre-action|transition|handoff \\\n263\t  [--rebound-at RFC3339] [--json]\n264\tharnessctl pr-body [TARGET] --artifact WO-... [--json]\n265\tharnessctl check [TARGET] [--artifact WO-...|VREC-...|RLS-...] [--json] [--include-background]  # without a checkpoint: the projection\n266\tharnessctl check [TARGET] --artifact WO-... --planned-path PATH [--planned-path PATH ...] [--json]\n267\tharnessctl check [TARGET] --artifact WO-...|VREC-...|RLS-... \\\n268\t  --checkpoint start|pre-action|transition|handoff|scope [--target STATE] \\  # with a checkpoint:\n269\t  [--procedure PROC-...] [--from-git BASE | --changed-path PATH ... \\\n270\t  [--changes-complete] | --change-manifest PATH] [--pull-request-body PATH] [--json]\n271\tharnessctl transition [TARGET] --set ID=STATUS --decision ID=ACTOR \\\n272\t  [--set ID=STATUS ...] [--decision ID=ACTOR ...] [--reason ID=TEXT ...] \\\n273\t  [--apply] [--json]\n274\t```\n275\t\n276\t`check` without `--checkpoint` is the one call an agent makes first (`WO-ECP-001`,\n277\tfolded from `next` by `WO-ECP-019`). It returns the projection of the selected artifact — the single\n278\t`in_progress` work order when `--artifact` is absent, otherwise `WEX-ECP-001` names the candidate\n279\tcount — with an additive `context` object: `reading_manifest` (the preflight manifest for the\n280\tphase the state implies, `start` for `approved` and `in_progress`, `review` afterwards),\n281\t`governing`, `declared_paths`, `state`, `next` (`argv`, `procedure_id`, `step_id`, the same step a\n282\tcheckpoint `check` selects) and `decision_required`. It writes nothing and needs no prior command.\n283\tThe human block renders the context as a `Context` section after `Command or response`, and\n284\t`result_sha256` binds it. The former `next` command was removed after 0.11.0 (`WO-ECP-020`); its\n285\ttombstone guard left with 0.15.0 (`WO-ECP-025`), so the parser now refuses the name as unknown.\n286\t\n287\t`check` without `--checkpoint` projects only the selected artifact's governing chain and direct\n288\tlifecycle dependencies. It uses the ordered recommendation registry in\n289\t`WORKFLOW.json`. For example, `WFL-WO-READY-VREC` takes precedence over\n290\t`WFL-WO-PREPARE-VREC`, so existing ready assurance coverage cannot produce a\n291\tduplicate-capture recommendation. Unrelated repository findings remain a\n292\tbackground count; `--include-background` expands categories without making\n293\tthem selected-scope work.\n294\t\n295\tThe optional `--planned-path` view assesses proposed files before approval.\n296\tIt requires an explicit work order and no checkpoint. Repeat the option for\n297\teach repository-relative file in the plan; the file need not exist yet.\n298\tExisting calls without this option are unchanged.\n299\t\n300\tThe schema-2 result adds `scope.preparation`: `planned_paths`, `coverage`\n301\t(`covered`, `uncovered` or `invalid`), `explicit_matches` with the matching\n302\t`scope_entry`, `automatic_matches` with the existing admission rule,\n303\t`uncovered_paths`, `invalid_declarations` and\n304\t`impact_analysis: \"not_assessed\"`. These machine fields participate in the\n305\tresult digest. The human report lists coverage and each path's reason.\n306\t\n307\tThe normal lifecycle projection, next action, exit meaning and gate fields\n308\tare preserved. **Exit zero does not mean the plan is covered.** Inspect\n309\t`scope.preparation.coverage` and resolve uncovered or invalid paths before\n310\trequesting approval. Coverage cannot prove that the agent found every\n311\taffected file. Planning writes nothing and does not populate actual changed\n312\tpaths, assert completeness, evaluate gates or authorize work.\n313\t\n314\tThe selected WO file and existing directly linked VREC/RLS records and their\n315\tdeclared evaluator evidence use their existing exact-path admission rules.\n316\tThe selected WO's own packet directory is reported separately under its\n317\texisting admission rule.\n318\tAn unallocated future record has no assessable path; explain its expected\n319\trelationship rule and check the actual destination after preparation.\n320\tOther review/log evidence needs explicit scope unless an existing rule covers\n321\tit. A neighboring file is not admitted by a generated record's directory.\n322\t\n323\tDo not combine planned paths with `--checkpoint`, `--target`, `--procedure`,\n324\t`--changed-path`, `--changes-complete`, `--change-manifest`, `--from-git`\n325\tor `--pull-request-body`. Invalid selection, malformed paths, case duplicates,\n326\tdirectory inputs and repository escapes are refused through normal diagnostics.\n327\tThis option must be used with a released evaluator that provides it; candidate\n328\tsource tests do not change the repository's selected evaluator.\n329\t\n330\tWith a checkpoint, `check` resolves the first matching rule, its typed `PROC-*` procedure, and its\n331\t`QG-*` gates; `--checkpoint scope` evaluates only the scope predicates of\n332\t`QG-G4-IMPLEMENTATION-EVIDENCE` for a work order in any lifecycle state and\n333\twrites nothing, which is what the managed pull-request gate runs (`WO-ECP-013`); [`harnessctl check` explained](harnessctl-check.md) walks\n334\tthrough the checkpoints, the rule table, the gates, and the refusal codes. `--checkpoint transition --target STATE` previews, read-only, the\n335\texact predicates and graph-structural checks `transition --set ID=STATE` will\n336\tevaluate (`WO-ECP-009`): the transition binding index of `QUALITY_GATES.json`\n337\tkeyed by artifact family and target state, evaluated by the same gate evaluator\n338\twith the same context, plus the `QGS-*` checks under the synthetic\n339\t`QG-STRUCTURAL` gate. A transition whose evaluation is not all `pass` renders\n340\t`Blocked by` with each refusing predicate's own identifier and writes nothing;\n341\tan applied transition that would be blocked fails closed with that identifier. `pre-action` requires `--procedure`, which must equal the selected\n342\tprocedure or one complete declared alternative. `--changed-path` may repeat;\n343\t`--changes-complete` asserts that the supplied set is complete, including an\n344\tempty set. The assertion is evidence, not proof from a trusted Git baseline.\n345\tWithout it, path-scope predicates are `not_assessable`.\n346\t\n347\t`--from-git BASE` derives the change set from Git instead of from typed\n348\tpaths: the union of `git diff --name-only BASE` against the working tree\n349\t(renames contribute both names) and the untracked files Git does not ignore,\n350\teach normalized as above; the set is complete by construction and the result\n351\trecords `change_set_source = \"git\"`. It is mutually exclusive with the\n352\tchanged-path options and the manifest (`WEX-ECP-002`); outside a Git\n353\tcheckout, with a base Git cannot resolve, or on any Git failure it blocks\n354\twith `WEX-ECP-003` and evaluates no predicate as `pass`. The selected work\n355\torder's own artifact file, written by its lifecycle transitions and so always\n356\tin the diff, is admitted to its scope by construction (`ECP-CHG-007`).\n357\t\n358\t`evidence` writes `DOMAIN/evidence/WO-ID/WO-ID-CHECKPOINT.md` (`WO-ECP-002`):\n359\ta fenced TOML header at byte offset 0 with exactly `artifact`, `checkpoint`,\n360\t`formal_snapshot_sha256` and `rebound_at`, followed by an owner-authored\n361\tbody. On an existing packet only the header bytes change; the body is\n362\tretained byte for byte, and a file without a header at offset 0, with a\n363\theader naming another artifact or checkpoint, or with invalid TOML is refused\n364\t(`WEX-ECP-010`). It refuses when a `.gitattributes` rule would convert the\n365\tpacket's line endings (`WEX-ECP-011`) and when the single `in_progress` work\n366\torder is not the one named (`WEX-ECP-012`). `QGP-G4I-EVIDENCE` reads that\n367\theader through a TOML parser; a packet without one is not assessable, and\n368\tthe message names the `evidence` command that writes the header (the\n369\tone-release substring grace closed under `WO-AUT-006`). `check --checkpoint handoff\n370\t--from-git BASE` is self-binding (`ECP-SBH-001` to `-006`): it rebinds an\n371\texisting packet header to the current formal snapshot before evaluating —\n372\tbody preserved, `evidence`'s `WEX-ECP-010`/`WEX-ECP-011` guards unchanged,\n373\tno packet created — and evaluates the change set with the retained result\n374\tpath included, so one run is the declared, digest-stable result. A\n375\tcompleted run retains its schema-2 result as `handoff.json` in the same\n376\tdirectory, written by the harness; that directory is admitted to the work\n377\torder's scope by construction.\n378\t\n379\t`pr-body` emits the pull-request body for an approved or later work order\n380\t(`WEX-ECP-014` otherwise): the standalone `Harness-Work-Order` line first, one\n381\tstandalone `Harness-Restitution` line carrying the retained `handoff.json`'s\n382\t`result_sha256` when it exists, then the seeded `## Summary` and\n383\t`## Verification` headings with every evidence path under the packet\n384\tdirectory. LF line endings only; the body round-trips through\n385\t`select-work-order` unchanged, so paste its output rather than typing it.\n386\t\n387\t`--change-manifest` is mutually exclusive with both changed-path options. It\n388\tmust be an in-repository UTF-8 JSON object containing only `schema` with value\n389\t`se-harness-change-set-v1`, Boolean `complete`, and ordered array `paths`.\n390\tPaths use `/`, exact-file or component-boundary directory-prefix matching, and\n391\treject absolute, traversal, backslash, wildcard, drive, URI, control-character,\n392\treserved-device, duplicate, and case-ambiguous forms.\n393\t\n394\t`check` always emits `se-harness-workflow-result-v2`. That structured result is\n395\tauthoritative. The deterministic direct human renderer uses `Outcome`, `Done`,\n396\t`Not done`, conditional `Blocked by`, `Current lifecycle state`, `Decision\n397\trequired`, `Next`, `Command or response`, and conditional `Alternatives` in\n398\tthat order. Exact-format consumers must use this renderer directly rather than\n399\task a model to transcribe it. `check`, `transition`, `capture-verification`,\n400\tand `prepare-release` emit the same `se-harness-workflow-result-v2` result\n401\tthrough one selector (`WO-ECP-005`); the former `--result-schema` option is\n402\tgone and passing it is an argument error. Each rule in `WORKFLOW.json` carries\n403\tonly the `done` and `current_lifecycle_state` prose of its restitution; the\n404\tnext step and the command come from the bound procedure.\n405\t\n406\tWhen `check` is blocked, `Next` and `Command or response` carry the corrective\n407\tform the contract declares for the first failing predicate: a command that\n408\tdiffers from the evaluated one (for example the handoff check with\n409\t`--changed-path` and `--changes-complete`), an escalation naming a decision\n410\tright, or a response describing the evidence to retain. The evaluated command\n411\tis never rendered as its own retry. Every schema-2 result carries\n412\t`result_sha256`. New results declare `digest_format = \"machine-fields-v1\"`\n413\tand hash stable machine fields rather than human wording. Retained results\n414\twithout the marker keep their original human-block digest; a pull-request body may declare it on one standalone\n415\t`Harness-Restitution:` line for CI to recompute. At `handoff`, a work order\n416\twhose `ready` verification record binds a commit no longer reachable from\n417\t`HEAD` is blocked with `W-ADS-002`; `--pull-request-body` additionally reports\n418\t`W-ADS-001` when the work-order trailer ends with a carriage return.\n419\t\n420\tAn agent-facing handoff may adapt wording, ordering, headings, and relevant\n421\texplanation or omit empty fields. It remains conforming only when it preserves\n422\tactual artifact IDs, outcome, observed effects, incomplete work, material\n423\tnon-effects, blockers, final lifecycle state, the accountable decision,\n424\tcommand argument boundaries or suggested-response meaning, and exactly one\n425\trecommended next action. Workflow-declared alternatives remain separate from\n426\tthat recommendation. Agent prose never becomes lifecycle authority.\n427\t\n428\t`transition` resolves IDs from formal metadata and plans by default. Each\n429\tselected ID needs one actor assertion. Rejection needs a non-empty reason; VREC\n430\tsupersession uses the reason as the exact successor VREC ID. A packet is\n431\tassessed as one proposed final graph. `--apply` rechecks every input byte,\n432\tproves the locked released-evaluator authority before writing, stages\n433\tsame-filesystem replacements outside artifact discovery, and rolls back earlier\n434\treplacements if a later write fails.\n435\t\n436\tThe command records actor text as an assertion, not proof of authority. The\n437\teffects and non-effects for each state are defined only by the matching\n438\t`WORKFLOW.json` rule. Related artifacts require separate explicit selection,\n439\tpassing gates, and authority.\n440\t\n441\tDirect human and JSON output are rendered from the same semantic workflow\n442\tresult. Schema 2 always identifies exactly one typed next step and derives its\n443\tcommand argument array or response from the selected procedure. Adaptive agent\n444\tpresentation consumes that result; it does not replace or recompute it.\n445\t\n446\t## Decision disposition\n447\t\n448\t```text\n449\tharnessctl decide [TARGET] --artifact DEC-... --option OPTION-ID --decision ACTOR [--authority-owner OWNER] --reason TEXT [--revisit TEXT] [--apply] [--json]\n450\tharnessctl decide [TARGET] --artifact DEC-... --defer --scope ARTIFACT-ID:FROM-TO ... --revisit TEXT --decision ACTOR [--authority-owner OWNER] --reason TEXT [--apply]\n451\tharnessctl decide [TARGET] --artifact DEC-... --withdraw --decision ACTOR [--authority-owner OWNER] --reason TEXT [--apply]\n452\t```\n453\t\n454\tA decision artifact (`DEC-`) records one pending question, or one implementation deviation from one rule of one specification. While it is `open`, every artifact named in its `blocks` relation is refused its transitions by the `QGP-*-DECISION` predicate of the gate that transition would pass. The refusal names the decision, its question, its options, the deciding role, and the `decide` command that clears it.\n455\t\n456\t`decide` is the only way a decision changes state; `transition` refuses it. Without `--apply` the command plans and reports; with `--apply` it writes the `[disposition]` table (the option, its label, the actual human, the time, and the verbatim reason) and one lifecycle event. `--option` must name one of the options the artifact declares. A deferral needs one `--scope` entry per transition it admits and a `--revisit` trigger; the scoped transitions pass, every other blocked transition still waits. Accepting a deviation needs `--revisit`, because acceptance is time-bounded. An ineligible owner is refused with `DR-DECISION-DISPOSE`.\n457\t\n458\t`--decision ACTOR` records the actual human who made the decision. With\n459\t`--authority-owner OWNER`, the evaluator checks OWNER against the existing\n460\tholders for the blocked artifacts, or the departed specification for a\n461\tdeviation. OWNER must match exactly and contain non-blank printable text of\n462\tat most 128 characters. It is retained separately as `authority_owner` in\n463\tthe disposition. Without the option, ACTOR must directly match a holder.\n464\tBoth preview and apply use the same checks. The CLI does not authenticate\n465\tthese claims or grant consent; the caller must first establish the human's\n466\tauthority and obtain the exact decision. Existing owner labels and historical\n467\trecords are not changed.\n468\t\n469\tThe validator reports a malformed decision as `E-DCM-001` to `E-DCM-003`, prose in a legacy definition's `## Open decisions` section as `E-DCM-004`, a deviation whose `against` fragment is not a rule identifier of the named specification (`SPEC-xxx#PREFIX-AREA-NNN`) as `E-DCM-005`, and an accepted deviation past its revisit or accepted twice against the same rule as `W-DCM-001` and `W-DCM-002`. See [decision artifacts](decision-artifacts.md) for the model.\n470\t\n471\tWhen the decision concerns a raised risk, `--apply` also moves that risk to the state the option names, in the same act: `accept` needs `--revisit`, `mitigate` needs `--mitigated-by WO-...`, and `avoid` records `--avoided-by` (an ADR or a decision; it defaults to the disposing decision). A deferral leaves the risk `raised`; a withdrawal withdraws it.\n472\t\n473\t## Risk recording\n474\t\n475\t```text\n476\tharnessctl raise-risk [TARGET] --domain SLUG --title TEXT --stage STAGE --category CATEGORY --cause TEXT --effect TEXT --likelihood N --impact N --threatens ID [--threatens ID ...] --raised-by ACTOR [--owner ROLE ...] [--id RISK-...] [--with-decision [--decision-id DEC-...] [--recommend accept|avoid|mitigate]] [--dry-run] [--json]\n477\tharnessctl risks [TARGET] --artifact ID [--json]\n478\t```\n479\t\n480\tA risk artifact (`RISK-`) records one measured threat: one cause, one effect, the stage it threatens, `likelihood` and `impact` from 1 to 5, and their product as `score`. `raise-risk` computes the score, writes the file in `raised` and records the raise as a lifecycle event, in one act; a measurement outside the range or an identifier already declared anywhere is refused before anything is written, exit 2. `--domain` takes the domain slug or the identifier token of exactly one domain. With `--with-decision` the command also writes the open decision that blocks the threatened artifacts, with the options `accept`, `avoid` and `mitigate`. No gate reads risks: the stop is the paired decision's `QGP-*-DECISION` predicate, and the refusal names the decision, not the risk.\n481\t\n482\t`risks` lists every risk threatening the named artifact or, for a work order, its governing chain; it writes nothing.\n483\t\n484\tThe validator reports a missing or invalid field as `E-RSK-001`, a wrong measurement or score as `E-RSK-002`, a raised risk that no pending decision names as `E-RSK-003`, a paired decision whose `blocks` differs from the risk's `threatens` as `E-RSK-004`, a disposition typed by hand as `E-RSK-005`, and an accepted risk past its revisit as `W-RSK-001`. See [risk artifacts](risk-artifacts.md) for the model.\n485\t\n486\t## Safe repository upgrade\n487\t\n488\t```text\n489\tharnessctl upgrade [TARGET] [--json]\n490\tharnessctl upgrade [TARGET] --apply [--json]\n491\tharnessctl upgrade [TARGET] --apply --work-order WO-... --evidence-output docs/engineering/DOMAIN/evidence/WO-...-evaluator-upgrade.json [--json]\n492\t```\n493\t\n494\tThe first form is a read-only plan. `--apply` is an explicit transactional repository mutation. Same-identity managed repair needs no new lifecycle packet. When the installed target evaluator differs from the standard lock, apply additionally requires a distinct approved or in-progress work order with an exact `[evaluator_upgrade]` packet and a work-order-keyed JSON evidence path. The packet binds the prior lock SHA-256 and exact immutable target archive/payload identity with `scope = \"standard-root-only\"`; a product release decision cannot substitute for it.\n495\t\n496\tApply requires the already-published target evaluator installed from exact wheel bytes outside the checkout, changes only eligible managed content, and stops without a partial managed update when identity, authority, customization, or conflict prevents a safe plan. Transition evidence, managed files, and the lock share the recoverable transaction, and successful replay must be a no-op. Every repository, including the `se_harness` implementation repository, follows this transaction and uses one exact released evaluator. GitHub discovers the managed workflow beside existing repository-owned workflows, while required-check and workflow-ordering policy remains external. See [installation and safe upgrades](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md).\n497\t\n498\t## Retained skill ownership\n499\t\n500\t```text\n501\tharnessctl skill-ownership TARGET --provider plugin --plugin-root DIRECTORY [--apply] [--json]\n502\tharnessctl skill-ownership TARGET --provider repository [--apply] [--json]\n503\t```\n504\t\n505\tThis candidate command is unavailable in released 0.17.0. It removes the two\n506\tnamed harness skill directories under .agents/skills and .claude/skills,\n507\tincluding edits and extra files. Other skill directories remain unchanged.\n508\tThe replacement must contain a Verity Plane manifest and the six required files.\n509\tPreview is optional. Apply reads current inputs, deletes the old copies, and\n510\tsaves the portable provider choice last. Rerun the command after an interruption.\n511\tRestoration copies the current repository templates over disposable old copies.\n512\tThis file-only operation grants no lifecycle authority and does not install a\n513\tplugin or change host settings. See [the current design](plugin-simplification-2026-09-13.md).\n514\t\n515\t## Predecessor-to-successor migration rehearsal\n516\t\n517\tThe former `rehearse-recovery` command is retired (`WO-ECP-030`, issue #376; it had no workflow caller and no retained report), as the former `rehearse-migration` command was (`WO-ECP-010`, issue #210); the root-evaluator handover is rehearsed by `python -m repository_tools.upgrade_rehearsal`, a repository-owned tool described in [rehearsing the root-evaluator handover](evaluator-migration-rehearsal.md), not by a `harnessctl` subcommand.\n518\t\n519\t\n520\t## Domain and artifact authoring\n521\t\n522\t```text\n523\tharnessctl scaffold-domain [TARGET] --domain DOMAIN [--title TITLE] [--dry-run] [--json]\n524\tharnessctl create-artifact [TARGET] --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE [--id ID] [--dry-run] [--quiet] [--json]\n525\t```\n526\t\n527\tDomain slugs, artifact identifiers, type prefixes, templates, and destinations are validated before mutation. `create-artifact` creates only an incomplete `draft`; it does not choose owners, relations, content, approval, or authority. After creation it prints the created type's checklist from `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`, resolved in the selected wheel for the external layout or in the repository for a supported older layout; `--quiet` suppresses it. Existing valid flat layouts remain discoverable and are not automatically migrated.\n528\t\n529\tWithout `--id`, `create-artifact` allocates the lowest free\n530\t`TYPE-DOMAIN-NNN` across every local branch and tag and the working tree,\n531\tuntracked files included (`WO-ECP-002`): the refs are enumerated with\n532\t`git for-each-ref` and each ref's `docs/engineering` tree is listed, so two\n533\tagents on two branches cannot take the same number; remote-tracking refs are\n534\tnot consulted. The domain token is read from the domain's existing\n535\tartifacts. The result names the refs on which the next-lower identifier was\n536\tfound, so a gap is explained. Outside a Git checkout allocation is refused\n537\t(`WEX-ECP-013`) rather than guessed from the working tree. An explicit `--id`\n538\tis refused when any local ref already carries it.\n539\t\n540\tNon-dry-run authoring uses the common pre-write mutation guard. The invoking environment must match the schema-3 released-evaluator identity locked by the target repository; candidate source and editable or contaminated installs fail without creating the requested path.\n541\t\n542\t## Release unit derivation\n543\t\n544\t```text\n545\tharnessctl release-unit [TARGET] --from TAG --to COMMIT [--exempt SHA ...] [--contract REL-ID] [--json | --toml]\n546\t```\n547\t\n548\tMeasures the work-order trailers between the previous release tag and a\n549\tcandidate commit, including merged work. The JSON shape remains compatible.\n550\tUntraced commits, incomplete census information, and contract differences are\n551\tadvisory and exit successfully; invalid Git refs or command inputs still fail.\n552\t`--exempt` remains readable for old invocations but is unnecessary. The owner\n553\tapproves final release scope, and the final candidate still needs verification.\n554\t\n555\t## Runtime identity\n556\t\n557\t```text\n558\tharnessctl identity --role released-evaluator|candidate-source|candidate-package \\\n559\t  --expected-version VERSION --expected-root PATH [options] [--json]\n560\t```\n561\t\n562\tKey role-specific options are `--checkout-root`, `--candidate-commit`, `--evaluator-wheel-sha256`, `--entry-point`, `--require-isolated-python`, and `--require-entry-point`. The command verifies declared runtime origin; it does not select an evaluator or approve a candidate.\n563\t\n564\tRuntime identity also observes the running interpreter's own entry-point path through the declared interpreter-safety rule and records three additional facts: whether the entry point is a symbolic link, which position class its resolved target occupies relative to the expected and checkout roots, and the target's SHA-256. The schema identifier stays `se-harness-runtime-identity-v3`, because consumers require a subset of the identity rather than an exact field set. The observation is recorded for every role, but only the two environment-bounded roles — `released-evaluator` and `candidate-package` — turn a refusal into the `RID024` diagnostic; `candidate-source` has no environment boundary, because its expected root is the checkout itself. `RID004` and `RID006` keep their existing meanings unchanged.\n565\t\n566\t## Role-specific release qualification\n567\t\n568\t```text\n569\tharnessctl qualify released-root [ROOT] [--output PATH] [--json]\n570\tharnessctl qualify complete-candidate [ROOT] --candidate-commit FULL_COMMIT [--output PATH] [--json]\n571\tharnessctl qualify candidate-package --candidate-wheel PATH --candidate-commit FULL_COMMIT --candidate-wheel-sha256 SHA256 --verifier-wheel-sha256 SHA256 [--checkout-root PATH] [--output PATH] [--json]\n572\tharnessctl qualify public-install [ROOT] --release-record RLS-... --public-wheel PATH --public-wheel-sha256 SHA256 --payload-sha256 SHA256 [--output PATH] [--json]\n573\t```\n574\t\n575\tThe four subcommands are separate closed parsers. They bind evaluator identity, target identity, fixed checks, and one independence class before reporting a result. They do not accept a general evaluator, validator, script, omission, or diagnostic-allowlist option. `--output` must name a new external file; the command never overwrites it or writes qualification evidence inside the inspected repository.\n576\t\n577\t`--evaluator-python` is judged by the declared interpreter-safety rule before anything is spawned. Supply the environment's own lexical entry point — `bin/python` on POSIX, `Scripts/python.exe` on Windows — not the resolved system interpreter it points at. The environment root is derived from that lexical path, so an interpreter reached through a linked or junctioned parent directory is refused, as is one inside the inspected checkout or whose resolved target lands inside it. The terminal interpreter link itself is permitted, which is what makes an ordinary `python -m venv` environment usable on POSIX.\n578\t\n579\tAll operations emit `se-harness-release-qualification-v1`. See [release qualification roles](release-qualification-roles.md) for the workflow map. `WO-REB-028` retired a fifth operation, `predecessor-view`, with the predecessor-bootstrap release path; its `PV001` and `PV002` codes stay reserved and no code path emits them.\n580\t\n581\tThe pre-namespace `accept-candidate` entry point, kept as a one-cycle alias of `qualify\n582\tcandidate-package` under `REQ-REB-022`, was removed after 0.11.0 (`WO-ECP-019`); its tombstone guard left with\n583\t0.15.0 (`WO-ECP-025`), so the parser now refuses the name as unknown.
