  "content": "1\t{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-final40-20261012\\\\claude-361\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"892ec2fedefc272f6bc2580268395e487f392cf5d92a3ea81fac015761bc87a8\", \"bytes\": 8641, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"links-from-work-orders-wo\", \"title\": \"Links from work orders (WO)\", \"anchor\": \"links-from-work-orders-wo\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 28, \"content\": \"## Links from work orders (WO)\\n\\nA work order (WO) selects the definitions and verification contracts (VER) that govern\\nits execution. Links to requirements (REQ) alone are not enough.\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `implements` | Names every requirement (REQ) in the authorized work scope. |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Specification (SPEC) | `specifications` | Names the specifications (SPEC) governing those requirements (REQ). |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Architecture (ARCH) or Architecture decision (ADR) | `architecture` | Names every applicable architecture (ARCH) and every required architecture decision (ADR). |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Verification contract (VER) | `verification` | Names the verification contracts (VER) for the work. |\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) can declare these links in its metadata. The IDs\\nbelow are examples, not records created by this document.\\n\\n```toml\\n[relations]\\nimplements = [\\\"REQ-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\nspecifications = [\\\"SPEC-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\nverification = [\\\"VER-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\n```\\n\\nThe referenced requirement (REQ) must also link back to a capability (CAP) and intent (INT).\\nAdd architecture (ARCH) links when architecture (ARCH) applies; do not invent them just to\\nfill a field.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e5892787048f79f437b0395f9e1269152ce3d1d1b6fb28994f42849bd12a4f54\"}, {\"heading\": \"complete-work-scope\", \"title\": \"Complete work scope\", \"anchor\": \"complete-work-scope\", \"start_line\": 47, \"end_line\": 65, \"content\": \"## Complete work scope\\n\\nEvery requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO)\\nMUST link back to active capabilities (CAP) and intents (INT). It MUST also\\nhave selected active specifications (SPEC) and verification contracts (VER).\\nReuse existing artifacts where their scope applies.\\n\\nA work order should cover one complete bounded outcome, including its\\nforeseeable tests, documentation and retained evidence. Use exact file paths\\nby default. Use a narrow existing component directory when the affected\\nfiles belong to that component. A matching directory does not authorize\\nunrelated behavior.\\n\\nPrepare this scope through\\n[Draft work orders](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements).\\nDo not split predictable supporting changes into extra work orders merely\\nbecause they use different file types. A genuine expansion after approval\\nstill needs the applicable human decision; preserve the approved history.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"021ca3cdecffebe415ce9df445c0c48e24a0acde7609d25220c0fb7d470e054e\"}, {\"heading\": \"assurance-classification\", \"title\": \"Assurance classification\", \"anchor\": \"assurance-classification\", \"start_line\": 86, \"end_line\": 116, \"content\": \"## Assurance classification\\n\\nEach work order (WO) in `approved` or\\n`in_progress` MUST set `assurance.commit_bound_verification` to `required`\\nor `not_required`.\\n\\nUse `required` when later decisions depend on the correctness of changes to\\ncode, required checks, CI configuration, harness policy, artifact definitions,\\nor their links. These are examples of \\u201cchanged trusted state\\u201d: information or\\nbehavior that others will rely on when accepting, releasing, or operating the\\nresult.\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) changes the code that validates artifact links.\\nA later release decision relies on that validation being correct. The work\\norder (WO) therefore needs verification tied to its exact candidate commit.\\n\\nUse `not_required` only when the work solely records or transports a\\nverification, release, supersession, publication, or deployment decision\\nthat an authorized human has already made. It does not make a new decision\\nor change the definitions, implementation, or evidence behind that decision.\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) commits an already authorized release decision\\nin a release record (RLS), with no change to the released code, scope, or\\nsupporting evidence. The work records the decision; it does not reassess the\\nrelease.\\n\\nA work order (WO) that combines both kinds of work MUST be split or classified\\n`required`. `not_required` removes the obligation to prepare a new\\nverification record (VREC) for that work; it does not remove required checks\\nor the links to verification contracts (VER).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6ad947ba93cfc84640c82a0b165448ce2c15f04beed36f65a3dc031e4287aab3\"}, {\"heading\": \"generated-outputs\", \"title\": \"Generated outputs\", \"anchor\": \"generated-outputs\", \"start_line\": 66, \"end_line\": 85, \"content\": \"## Generated outputs\\n\\nExisting scope rules admit the selected work order's own file, records that\\ndirectly verify or release that work order, and those records' declared\\nevaluator-evidence paths. This does not admit those records' parent directories.\\nThe selected work order's own packet directory is also already admitted by\\nthe existing scope rules; the planning report identifies that separate rule.\\n\\nList other planned evidence, review and log destinations explicitly in the\\nwork order's scope unless an existing rule covers them. A neighboring file\\nor a record linked only to another work order is not automatically admitted.\\nThe conditional rule for recording risks during execution remains unchanged;\\nit is not a blanket admission of future files during preparation.\\n\\nIf a future record's ID is not allocated, mark its destination as unresolved\\nand explain the relationship rule expected to cover it. Do not create a\\nrecord or invent an ID to complete the plan. Once the evaluator prepares\\nthe record, assess its actual returned record and evidence paths. An\\nunresolved destination is not an already covered file.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"21cb2760e5cf61158c5d19cca2af8dbe727ecf3df32247987cc1636059bde3e9\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-final40-20261012\\\\claude-361\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"991b526d6280554dcca6901c1790e5519b8894e08635a1f10618aa84a29aaf28\", \"bytes\": 15212, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nThe proposed package needs validation, review or a human authorization decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8b18d925f39f314acc9ea6bcc9820015c4c9430d836144e85bc31b670752371b\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nFor reviewing each definition, use its selected [Type checklist](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#type-checklists). Before review, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation). Before approving work, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). For an open or deferred decision, read [RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"9aa32693606102a5aa74b2e4a614aed6904471e5f618dea93356baac97c86ca2\"}, {\"heading\": \"assess-the-proposed-artifact-package\", \"title\": \"Assess the proposed artifact package\", \"anchor\": \"assess-the-proposed-artifact-package\", \"start_line\": 32, \"end_line\": 83, \"content\": \"### Assess the proposed artifact package\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected work order (WO) IDs, proposed definitions, validation\\nresults, and existing decision records (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None created or modified.\\n- **Transient working material:** A review list identifying the selected\\n  artifacts, their states, applicable checks, and reported blockers.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Run validation for the repository.\\n2. Inspect each selected work order (WO) with the command below.\\n3. Read the work order (WO) and its returned reading manifest.\\n4. Review the governing definitions against the relevant checklists in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n5. Check that the proposed work has defined scope, verification coverage,\\n   assurance classification, and accountable humans for the required decisions.\\n6. List the blockers affecting the selected package. Keep unrelated findings\\n   separate.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint transition --target approved --json\\n```\\n\\nRead the result of each required check. A `pass` satisfies that check only;\\nit does not approve the artifacts or authorize implementation. If a required\\ncheck returns `fail` or `not_assessable`, report its identifier and stated\\nreason, then follow \\u201cIf a procedure is blocked.\\u201d Do not proceed with the\\naffected approval.\\n\\nThe last command evaluates work-order approval gates. A checkpoint-free\\n`check` only reports lifecycle context. Definition artifacts cannot be selected\\nwith `check`; their transition gates are evaluated by the previews in [Apply the selected transitions](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#apply-the-selected-transitions).\\n\\nBefore proposing a definition for approval, resolve its template placeholders.\\nIf it contains an `Open decisions` section, confirm that no unresolved decision\\nremains before setting that section to `None`. Do not remove an unresolved\\nquestion merely to make validation pass.\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected package has an explicit list of review findings\\nand approval blockers. No approval is inferred from these checks.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Resolve approval blockers](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#resolve-approval-blockers) resolves the blockers. [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision) presents the package for a\\nhuman decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"2ea6b051236e13dd427317722d16ce7941ef5a4eb4789f7fdf568ab3d0cae3c0\"}, {\"heading\": \"apply-the-selected-transitions\", \"title\": \"Apply the selected transitions\", \"anchor\": \"apply-the-selected-transitions\", \"start_line\": 221, \"end_line\": 270, \"content\": \"### Apply the selected transitions\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact artifact IDs, target states, accountable human identities,\\nreviewed file digests, decisions from [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision), and clarification answers from\\n[Define the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#procedure) that must be retained in the transition reason.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only explicitly selected definitions and work orders\\n  (WO) receive the applied state and lifecycle-history entries.\\n- **Transient working material:** The preview and apply results, including\\n  any refused transition.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Confirm that the reviewed artifact contents still match the human decision.\\n2. Select only the named transitions. Approve governing definitions before\\n   dependent work, or use one explicitly selected packet for mutually\\n   dependent definitions when the evaluator permits it.\\n3. Preview the transition command below.\\n4. Compare every selected ID, target state, actor, and reported effect with\\n   the human decision. Resolve failed gates before proceeding.\\n5. Recheck reviewed definition digests immediately before applying.\\n6. Repeat the passing command with `--apply`. Do not add related artifacts\\n   that the human did not select.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set ARTIFACT-ID=TARGET --decision ARTIFACT-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set ARTIFACT-ID=TARGET --decision ARTIFACT-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\n```\\n\\nFor each clarification below the formal-decision threshold, add\\n`--reason \\\"ARTIFACT-ID=Question and confirmed answer\\\"` to both the preview\\nand apply command. Use the actual question and answer. When one artifact\\nhas several such answers, combine them into one reason value for that ID.\\nKeep each complete `ID=TEXT` value as one argument. Confirm the saved reason\\nin the resulting lifecycle entry before discarding the working notes.\\n\\nFor approval, `TARGET` is `approved`. For rejection, use `rejected` and add\\n`--reason \\\"ARTIFACT-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to both commands. Rejection is\\nterminal. For a packet, repeat `--set` and `--decision` for every explicitly\\nselected artifact. Preview and apply must contain the same assignments.\\n\\n**Completion:** The evaluator reports the actual applied transitions, or the\\nspecific refusal. A successful preview alone changes nothing.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Confirm the authorization result](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#confirm-the-authorization-result) confirms the resulting authority and readiness.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c5215dec9f35d1a99bf6e4d658a594a31dc544131e70db49b1b8f79514e124b8\"}, {\"heading\": \"resolve-approval-blockers\", \"title\": \"Resolve approval blockers\", \"anchor\": \"resolve-approval-blockers\", \"start_line\": 84, \"end_line\": 159, \"content\": \"### Resolve approval blockers\\n\\n**Inputs:** The findings from [Assess the proposed artifact package](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#assess-the-proposed-artifact-package) and the affected draft artifacts or\\npending decisions (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Corrected drafts within the proposed scope. Where an\\n  actual human decision is supplied, the selected decision (DEC) receives its\\n  disposition. A paired risk (RISK) may change through that same operation.\\n- **Transient working material:** The resolution of each finding and any\\n  remaining dependency requiring an amendment or another human decision.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Correct incomplete or inconsistent draft content within the requested scope.\\n2. Return an accepted-definition change to the amendment procedure in\\n   \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Do not edit accepted authority to clear a check.\\n3. For a blocking decision (DEC), inspect its current question and options.\\n4. Obtain the accountable human's exact answer if it has not already been given.\\n5. Preview that disposition with the command below.\\n6. Apply the same command with `--apply` only if its inputs match the actual\\n   decision and the preview passes.\\n7. Read back the decision (DEC) and any paired risk (RISK).\\n8. Rerun the checks affected by the corrections. Preserve unresolved blockers.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --option OPTION-ID --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nUse a declared option ID. Add `--revisit \\\"Trigger\\\"` for acceptance of a\\ndeviation. A risk-mitigation option also requires `--mitigated-by WO-ID` for\\neach selected mitigating work order (WO). For a risk-avoidance option, use\\n`--avoided-by ARTIFACT-ID` when naming a separate architecture decision (ADR)\\nor decision (DEC). Review the returned operation before applying it.\\n\\nACTOR is the actual human who made the decision. If that human acts under an\\nexisting owner label, first resolve their authority under\\n[Decision rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights), then add\\n`--authority-owner OWNER` to both preview and apply. For example, a human\\nnamed `mmzen` acting under `engineering-owner` uses\\n`--decision mmzen --authority-owner engineering-owner`. Do not put the owner\\nlabel in place of the human. Neither string authenticates the decision.\\nOWNER must be non-blank printable text of at most 128 characters and match\\nan eligible owner exactly. An unrelated label refuses without writing.\\n\\nFor an explicitly authorized deferral, use this preview instead:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --defer --scope ARTIFACT-ID:FROM-TO --revisit \\\"Trigger\\\" --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nRepeat `--scope` for each permitted transition. For an explicitly authorized\\nwithdrawal, replace the option or deferral arguments with `--withdraw`.\\nApply a passing preview by repeating the exact command with `--apply`.\\nThen inspect the decision (DEC) again and rerun validation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\nIf proposing a departure from a `SHOULD` rule, record the rule ID, reason,\\nimpact, accountable human or agent, and compensating evidence. Present these\\nwith the affected review finding. Recording the departure does not authorize\\nan action or waive a required check.\\n\\n**Completion:** Each blocker is resolved or assigned an explicit outstanding\\ndecision. A deferral clears only its recorded transition scope.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision) receives the corrected package. Unresolved blockers\\nremain visible and prevent the affected approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ead7ade46e1090c644d789a5ca1155415aa2497561938b885e8316cd13aeb920\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORITY.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-final40-20261012\\\\claude-361\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORITY.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"da7202bf8d1beee631e9b4b5ba01c04b440fbf76d200ccbccbb8781a59f88431\", \"bytes\": 16163, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"decision-rights\", \"title\": \"Decision rights\", \"anchor\": \"decision-rights\", \"start_line\": 19, \"end_line\": 80, \"content\": \"## Decision rights\\n\\nA profile describes who performs an action. A decision right describes which\\naction that person or agent is authorized to perform. Being a Human does not\\ngrant every right in this table. Being an Agent grants none by itself.\\n\\nUse the artifact's recorded ownership and any existing explicit delegation to\\nidentify the accountable human. Resolve a team name or ownership label to the\\nhuman making this decision. A proposed `owners` value, an example actor name,\\nor authorship of a draft MUST NOT assign decision authority.\\n\\nApproval, verification acceptance, and release decisions MUST be made by an\\nauthorized human. An agent MAY prepare the material and apply that human's\\nrecorded decision when authorized to do so. Applying the decision does not\\nmake the agent its author. The selected IDs, reviewed content, target states,\\nand reason MUST still match the decision at apply time.\\n\\nThe following stable IDs name rights and operations, not additional profiles.\\nAll applicable gates remain required.\\n\\nThese DR-* identifiers come from the selected evaluator's decision-right\\ncatalogue. Use the right and exact action returned by that evaluator. Legacy\\nowner labels identify recorded accountabilities; they do not create additional\\nHuman/Agent profiles or assign a decision to a person by themselves.\\n\\n| Right ID                   | Accountable profile and authority                                                                                                  | Required input                                                                                                    | Result                                                                                               |\\n|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `DR-DEFINITION-DECIDE`     | Human authorized to decide the selected definition.                                                                                | Complete definition, exact proposed state, and required checks.                                                   | Decision on that definition only.                                                                    |\\n| `DR-WO-SELECT`             | Human authorized to approve the work scope.                                                                                        | Complete governing chain, bounded work order, and assurance classification.                                       | Approval or rejection of the selected work order.                                                    |\\n| `DR-WO-START`              | Human or Agent executing the selected work under its recorded approval.                                                            | Unchanged approved scope and passing start checks.                                                                | The selected work order becomes `in_progress`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-WO-COMPLETE`           | Human or Agent executing the selected work under its recorded approval.                                                            | Completed scope, passing handoff checks, and retained evidence.                                                   | The selected work order becomes `implemented`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-VREC-PREPARE`          | Human or Agent under the approval of every selected work order.                                                                    | Exact candidate, selected work and verification contracts, retained evidence, and passing preparation checks.     | One `ready` verification record; no acceptance decision.                                             |\\n| `DR-VREC-DECIDE`           | Human authorized to accept verification for the selected candidate.                                                                | Ready record, assessed evidence, and the exact verify, reject, or supersede decision.                             | Decision on that verification record only.                                                           |\\n| `DR-DELIVERY-SELECT`       | Human authorized for the chosen integration or release-preparation path.                                                           | Exact candidate, destination, and coverage required by that path.                                                 | One path-specific instruction.                                                                       |\\n| `DR-RLS-PREPARE`           | Human authorizes the release inputs; a Human or Agent may carry out the preparation.                                               | Exact release contract, candidate, included work, verification coverage, version, and passing preparation checks. | One `ready` release record; no release decision.                                                     |\\n| `DR-RLS-DECIDE`            | Human authorized to make the release decision.                                                                                     | Ready release record, assessed contract obligations, and the exact release or reject decision.                    | Decision on that release record only.                                                                |\\n| `DR-EXTERNAL-ACTION`       | Human authorized for the exact external action. A Human or Agent may execute the authorized operation.                             | Action, immutable target, destination, prerequisites, and recovery conditions.                                    | Authorization limited to that operation; the subsequent tool result records its actual effects.      |\\n| `DR-RELATED-RECORD-SELECT` | Human or Agent; no decision authority is needed for inspection.                                                                    | Exact existing artifact ID.                                                                                       | Read-only selection.                                                                                 |\\n| `DR-REMEDIATION-SCOPE`     | Human authorized to change the affected definition or work scope.                                                                  | Failed criterion and proposed bounded correction.                                                                 | Explicit authority for the revised scope.                                                            |\\n| `DR-DECISION-DISPOSE`      | Human accountable for the artifact blocked by the decision; for a deviation, the human accountable for the affected specification. | Open or deferred decision, selected option or disposition, exact reason, and any required revisit trigger.        | Recorded disposition and any declared paired-risk effect. Other blocked artifacts keep their states. |\\n\\nFor a lifecycle decision, the `--decision` value identifies its actual\\ndecision-maker. When an agent applies a human decision, that value is the\\nhuman who made it. For start and completion under approved execution, it is\\nthe actual Human or Agent executor. Supplying either identity does not grant\\nauthority. Preparation `--owner` values identify the preparation actor, not\\na future assurance or release decision-maker.\\n\\nFor `decide`, when an owner label differs from the actual human's identity,\\nuse `--authority-owner OWNER` only after establishing that human's authority\\nfor the exact decision. Keep `--decision ACTOR` as the actual human. The\\nevaluator checks that OWNER holds the existing decision right and records it\\nseparately as `authority_owner`. With the option absent, ACTOR must itself\\nmatch an eligible owner. The command does not authenticate either claim or\\ngrant consent. Do not infer a binding from the decision's own owners, an\\nearlier approval, Git configuration or the agent's identity.\\n\\nSilence, elapsed time, a commit, a pull request, tool execution, or a passing\\ncheck MUST NOT count as a human decision. A rejection MUST include a non-empty\\nreason. Supersession MUST name exactly one eligible successor. The decision\\nand its resulting state MUST remain specific to the selected artifact.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6ecaeb29429bcaa4eac99857f2f921e270c4865d1edeec96f536d09eb6c3130a\"}, {\"heading\": \"delegation-and-separation\", \"title\": \"Delegation and separation\", \"anchor\": \"delegation-and-separation\", \"start_line\": 111, \"end_line\": 133, \"content\": \"## Delegation and separation\\n\\nA human decision right may be delegated only to another human who is permitted\\nto hold it. The delegation MUST name the right, its scope, the granting human,\\nand the receiving human. It MUST be recorded before the delegated decision.\\nThe receiving human MUST decide under their own identity.\\n\\nAn instruction for an agent to apply a recorded human decision delegates the\\nexecution of that command. It does not delegate the decision itself. The\\nagent MUST NOT supply a new answer, broaden the targets, or claim the human\\nmade a decision that was not given.\\n\\nRepository policy MAY require different people for conflicting decisions on\\nthe same candidate. When it does, the same human MUST NOT hold both decisions\\nfor that candidate. A human MUST NOT approve their own architecture decision\\nassessment unless they explicitly hold approval authority for that artifact\\nand the separation rules permit it. Drafting an assessment grants no such\\nright.\\n\\nWhen the accountable human or required authority is absent or ambiguous, stop\\nthe affected decision. State the exact right and artifact needing an owner.\\nDo not substitute an available human or agent merely to fill the field.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"f07389fbbe529ad544d8b7d7f18894bfa45f0ec69996c93ed8372416b55ddf91\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-final40-20261012\\\\claude-361\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"8dbc5fb4bb80fc3c2fbf1ec34a2419e8b5856972485226af46ae324fbd9aca5c\", \"bytes\": 11817, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nA risk or unresolved formal question affects the selected change.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"2c0226a6752c15139cda1b7192d98f116d9947c483e5c62826c624c81a55c11a\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore writing, read [Links for decisions and risks](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#links-for-decisions-and-risks), [Blocking decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions) and [Raised risks](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#raised-risks). Apply [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk) or [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision) for the selected record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8a14639d6c2512ed5f9bfea0f7bfd9d4a2e428642e8fc8a02d600f792ab846f\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change\", \"title\": \"Record risks (RISK) affecting the change\", \"anchor\": \"record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 65, \"content\": \"### Record risks (RISK) affecting the change\\n\\n**Inputs:** The outcome, scope, selected definitions, verification coverage,\\nand existing risks (RISK) found in [Identify the existing artifacts that apply to the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#identify-the-existing-artifacts-that-apply-to-the-change).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New risks (RISK) in `raised` for threats not already\\n  covered. A paired decision (DEC) in `open` for each risk created with\\n  `--with-decision`. None created where existing records cover the threats.\\n- **Transient working material:** The selection of reused risks (RISK),\\n  review notes, generated IDs and paths, and links awaiting new work order\\n  (WO) IDs. If no risks are identified, retain that result with the reviewed\\n  scope. Retain this material under the same conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Identify what could go wrong within the selected change scope.\\n2. Check whether an existing risk (RISK) already records each threat and its\\n   follow-up. Reference that record instead of creating a duplicate.\\n3. For each new risk (RISK), describe the threat and why it matters.\\n4. Identify its follow-up owner.\\n5. Specify the owner's next action.\\n6. Identify the formal artifacts threatened by it.\\n7. Determine whether an unresolved decision must block those artifacts.\\n8. Preview the risk (RISK) with the command below. Inspect the proposed\\n   content, affected IDs, and destination paths.\\n9. Run the same command with the same arguments, removing only `--dry-run`.\\n10. Read every written file reported by the command. Retain its ID and path\\n    for the review handoff.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\nReplace the quoted text and `OWNER` with the risk description and identified\\nowner. Repeat `--threatens ARTIFACT-ID` for each threatened artifact. Omit that\\noption if no affected formal artifact exists yet:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl raise-risk REPO --domain DOMAIN --title \\\"Risk title\\\" --description \\\"What could go wrong and why it matters\\\" --action \\\"Next follow-up action\\\" --owner OWNER --threatens ARTIFACT-ID --dry-run --json\\n```\\n\\nAdd `--with-decision` only if action 7 identifies a decision (DEC) that must\\nblock the named artifacts. Use the same option in both preview and creation.\\nA risk (RISK) alone does not block work.\\n\\n**Completion:** Identified risks (RISK) have formal records with an owner and\\nnext action. If none were identified, retain `None identified` with the\\nreviewed scope as transient working material.\\n\\n**Later use:** Review any paired decision (DEC) in [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec). [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements) uses the\\nrisks (RISK) to define work and stop conditions and adds links that depend on\\nnew work order (WO) IDs.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8431175790f8bf07019c19f9cb51d6ee5186b8bc66fccfbb2665ab99fc5028e9\"}, {\"heading\": \"raised-risks\", \"title\": \"Raised risks\", \"anchor\": \"raised-risks\", \"start_line\": 176, \"end_line\": 187, \"content\": \"## Raised risks\\n\\nA risk (RISK) in `raised` may have no paired decision\\n(DEC). Recording that risk alone does not block work. Use\\n`raise-risk --with-decision` when creating a risk that needs a paired blocking\\ndecision.\\n\\nA raised risk MUST NOT have more than one paired decision in `open` or\\n`deferred`. When that decision exists, it names the risk in `concerns`, and\\nits `blocks` set MUST equal the risk's `threatens` set. Disposing the paired\\ndecision applies its recorded effect to the risk in the same operation.\\nThe blocked artifacts change state only through their own transitions.\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"dcbef84857f6b71fbfa2099de79f6caa4d82e8977b13465eccb762ffc3a9ea1e\"}]}]}\n2\t"
}

Apply [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk) or [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision) for the selected record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8a14639d6c2512ed5f9bfea0f7bfd9d4a2e428642e8fc8a02d600f792ab846f\"}, {\"heading\": \"links-for-decisions-and-risks\", \"title\": \"Links for decisions and risks\", \"anchor\": \"links-for-decisions-and-risks\", \"start_line\": 132, \"end_line\": 149, \"content\": \"## Links for decisions and risks\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 any artifact type | `concerns` | Names every artifact the question is about. |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ), Specification (SPEC), Verification contract (VER), Architecture (ARCH), Architecture decision (ADR), or Work order (WO) | `blocks` | Names artifacts whose transitions the decision (DEC) blocks. Each must also appear in `concerns`. |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ), Specification (SPEC), Verification contract (VER), Architecture (ARCH), Architecture decision (ADR), or Work order (WO) | `produces` | A decision (DEC) in `decided` names artifacts its answer created or amended, when applicable. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 any artifact type | `threatens` | Names the artifacts the risk (RISK) could damage. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 Work order (WO) | `mitigated_by` | Names the work orders (WO) reducing a risk (RISK) in `mitigating` or `mitigated`. The decision operation writes this link. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 Architecture decision (ADR) or Decision (DEC) | `avoided_by` | Names the single architecture decision (ADR) or decision (DEC) that removes a risk (RISK) in `avoided`. The decision operation writes this link. |\\n\\nA decision (DEC) records a question that needs an answer or a proposed deviation.\\nAn architecture decision (ADR) records a settled design choice. They serve different purposes.\\n\\nA risk (RISK) does not block work by itself. When a blocking decision (DEC)\\nis requested, that decision (DEC) concerns the risk (RISK). The `blocks` set\\nof the decision (DEC) matches the `threatens` set of the risk (RISK).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"5009680651d50038248f4c60c5fceaf6065393bf7b3b2f370c54560ba83dd63a\"}, {\"heading\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"title\": \"Blocking decisions\", \"anchor\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"start_line\": 150, \"end_line\": 175, \"content\": \"## Blocking decisions\\n\\nA decision (DEC) in `open` blocks every transition\\nof the artifacts in its `blocks` relation. A decision (DEC) in `deferred`\\nblocks transitions outside its recorded permitted scope.\\n\\nFor example, a decision (DEC) names work order (WO) `WO-EXAMPLE-001` in both\\n`concerns` and `blocks`. It is deferred with the scope\\n`WO-EXAMPLE-001:approved-in_progress`. This deferral\\nallows the work order (WO) to move from `approved` to `in_progress` if all\\nother checks pass. It still blocks moving that work order (WO) from\\n`in_progress` to `implemented`. The deferral also records when the decision\\n(DEC) must be revisited. Deferral does not itself start the work.\\n\\nAn accepted deviation is a decision (DEC) with `kind = \\\"deviation\\\"`,\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"`, and `disposition.option = \\\"accept\\\"`.\\nIt records permission to depart from one identified specification (SPEC)\\nrule; \\u201caccepted\\u201d is not a separate lifecycle state for the decision (DEC).\\n\\nThat deviation remains applicable to the affected specification (SPEC),\\nwork orders (WO), and their verification records (VREC) and release records\\n(RLS) until a later decision (DEC) against the same rule reaches\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"` with `disposition.option` set to `amend` or\\n`supersede`. The disposition is written through `harnessctl decide`, not\\nby editing the metadata by hand.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ed29cb785085f0704b9ab61f95ab42f2ee01579c0d191cb6587ce6c97684cdc0\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-final40-20261012\\\\claude-361\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"risk\", \"title\": \"risk\", \"anchor\": \"risk\", \"start_line\": 188, \"end_line\": 198, \"content\": \"## risk\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Record a description, an owner and a next action.\\n- Use `harnessctl raise-risk --description TEXT --action TEXT --owner ROLE` with a domain and title.\\n- Stage, category, threatened artifacts and scoring are optional. If scoring is useful, supply likelihood and impact together (1\\u20135); the command computes their product.\\n- Request `--with-decision` only when the owner needs a decision that blocks named artifacts. A risk by itself does not block work.\\n- Keep earlier scores, decisions and dispositions as recorded; no migration is required.\\n\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8815c9ff38ca34594404ab95cb0545053e209804030f3d635a50641d33559de9\"}, {\"heading\": \"decision\", \"title\": \"decision\", \"anchor\": \"decision\", \"start_line\": 171, \"end_line\": 187, \"content\": \"## decision\\n\\nA pending question becomes a `decision` (`DEC-`) when it blocks a transition\\nof another artifact, concerns more than one artifact, or must survive the\\napproval of the artifact that raised it. Below that threshold the actor asks\\nand the answer stays in the transition's `reason`.\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `kind` is `question` (an ambiguity met while authoring or planning) or `deviation` (an implementation cannot meet one rule of one specification). *(mechanical)*\\n- One `question`, `raised_by`, at least two `[[options]]` with `id` and `label`, and a `recommendation` naming one option. *(mechanical)*\\n- A deviation also names `against = \\\"SPEC-xxx#PREFIX-AREA-NNN\\\"`, a rule identifier the specification defines *(mechanical: E-DCM-005)*, and the `observed` fact; its options are drawn from `amend`, `supersede`, `accept`, `stop` and include `stop`. *(mechanical)*\\n- `concerns` names every artifact the question is about; `blocks` names the artifacts that cannot change state while it is `open`, each also in `concerns`. *(mechanical)*\\n- The `[disposition]` table is written by `harnessctl decide`; a hand-written one is `E-DCM-003`. A deferral needs a scope and a revisit trigger; accepting a deviation needs a revisit trigger. *(mechanical)*\\n- `decided` and `withdrawn` decisions are never deleted or rewritten.\\n- The definition templates carry no `Open decisions` section: a definition's pending decisions are the `DEC-` artifacts that name it in `blocks`, and the approval gate reads them from the graph. A legacy section, where one remains, reads `None` or lists `DEC-` identifiers; prose there is `E-DCM-004`.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"b3fdcc8578aac9039cf6513b13851f7a35a63027fde6dd1afeb34593a23e083b\"}]}]}",

Apply the same transition only when preflight and the preview pass.\\n5. Inspect the resulting state.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase start --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=in_progress --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=in_progress --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected work order (WO) is `in_progress`, or its start\\nis blocked with an explicit reason. Run every required check using its specified inputs and environment.\\n2. Retain the command arguments, working directory, runtime identity, exit\\n   status, output, and relevant file paths or digests.\\n3. Preserve failed results alongside later corrections and successful reruns.\\n4. Retain the material diff-review findings and their resolution.\\n5. Confirm that all required evidence files exist at the locations named by\\n   the work order (WO) or verification contract (VER).\\n6. Run review preflight.\\n7. Run the Git-derived handoff check with the trusted `BASE` from [Establish the execution context](EXECUTE_WORK.md#establish-the-execution-context).\\n8. Inspect its written evidence and reported findings. Correct in-scope gaps\\n   and rerun affected checks.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase review --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint handoff --from-git BASE --json\\n```\\n\\nFor ordinary files listed in the work order\\u2019s `evidence_paths`, confirm that\\neach file exists inside the repository and contains the required evidence.\\nThese files do not need a machine header. Confirm its output\\npaths are covered by the approved preparation scope. If the evaluator calls\\nfor creating or rebinding the handoff evidence packet, use:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl evidence REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint handoff --json\\n```\\n\\nThis command also writes a file. Rerun the required handoff check after correcting the evidence gap.\\n\\n**Completion:** Required implementation checks pass and the actual evidence\\nis retained, or the exact missing or failed checks remain visible.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Record implementation completion](EXECUTE_WORK.md#record-implementation-completion) requires passing handoff results. Verification later\\nassesses these retained files; they are not disposable planning notes.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"4cccfe03ac5fe219da997051bb91053576f18e67e834f0036f93e9856e8f12a2\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-implementation-completion\", \"title\": \"Record implementation completion\", \"anchor\": \"record-implementation-completion\", \"start_line\": 211, \"end_line\": 257, \"content\": \"### Record implementation completion\\n\\n**Inputs:** Completed work, passing handoff checks, retained evidence, and\\nthe unchanged approved execution scope.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** The selected work order (WO) becomes `implemented`\\n  with the actual executor recorded in its lifecycle history.\\n- **Transient working material:** The completion report and current next step.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. A Human\\nand an Agent MUST use the same local approval, scope, and evidence checks.\\nContinue these operations without asking for the same permission again while\\ntheir scope and conditions still match. Record execution under the actual\\nexecutor's identity.\\n\\nApproval leaves the work order `approved` until its start transition is\\napplied. Selecting and scheduling work remain explicit. New approvals need\\nno separate execution delegation table or second start approval. A preliminary\\nmerge and live CI are not local execution requirements; CI still applies at\\nintegration and publication.\\n\\nThe grant does not include changed scope, acceptance of the result, release,\\nmerge, publication, or other external action. Reuse an existing explicit\\nauthorization for such an action only when its exact target and conditions\\nstill match.\\n\\nHistorical approvals keep their original meaning. Earlier explicit execution\\ngrants remain usable under the same scope checks. Read the exact candidate and retained evidence required by the selected contract.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"509b10e8e12887c623b12e5997e2baf7bcb193b87a24b63fe19795676bddc8a7\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-the-verification-record\", \"title\": \"Prepare the verification record\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-the-verification-record\", \"start_line\": 108, \"end_line\": 169, \"content\": \"### Prepare the verification record\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact candidate, selected work orders (WO), their verification\\ncontracts (VER), retained evidence, and existing preparation authority.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** One new verification record (VREC) in `ready` when\\n  capture is required and succeeds. Related work-order (WO) states do not change.\\n- **Retained files:** The generated evaluator evidence and candidate snapshot\\n  or export required by the capture procedure.\\n- **Transient working material:** The capture result and inspected output paths.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. If a suitable verification record (VREC) already exists, inspect it and\\n   continue to [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision). Do not duplicate an interrupted successful capture.\\n2. Confirm preparation authority under every selected work order's (WO)\\n   approval. Reuse it while the scope and inputs match.\\n3. Select an unused `VREC-ID` after checking the repository's local Git refs.\\n4. Confirm the domain and actual record and evidence destinations. Keep all\\n   generated writes within the authorized preparation scope.\\n5. Establish a clean committed candidate using authorized local Git actions.\\n   Retain its full commit ID. Do not discard unrelated changes to obtain it.\\n6. Run the capture command with each selected work order (WO), every declared\\n   verification contract (VER), and each retained evidence file.\\n7. Read the generated record and evaluator evidence. Confirm the candidate\\n   commit, selected IDs, evidence digests, and `ready` state.\\n8. Retain generated records and evidence in a later authorized governance\\n   commit. Preserve the earlier candidate commit that the record assesses.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl capture-verification REPO --id VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --verification VER-ID --evidence EVIDENCE-PATH --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order`, `--verification`, and `--evidence` for every selected\\ninput. `EVIDENCE-PATH` is a repository-relative file, not a directory or an\\nindex whose links will be followed automatically. Capture writes immediately\\nafter its checks; it has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\nIf an unchanged rebase leaves an earlier ready record bound to the old\\ncandidate, use [Refresh verification after an unchanged rebase](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#refresh-verification-after-an-unchanged-rebase).\\nA verified source or changed relevant inputs cannot use that shortcut.\\n\\nIf preserving local edits requires the supported committed-candidate route,\\nuse `--candidate-commit COMMIT` with `--test-command EXECUTABLE ARGUMENTS`.\\nPut `--test-command` last. That route tests the named commit in a temporary\\ncheckout; use its actual results and returned record, not results from the\\nuncommitted edits.\\n\\n**Completion:** A ready verification record (VREC) binds the selected candidate\\nand evidence, or capture reports a specific refusal. Preparation is not verification.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) presents the exact record and evidence for the human decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"34e77e503346373221eaa0bb46e970ee738ce6a5eebbfdece9ba6e8ee36450a1\"}, {\"heading\": \"assess-the-verification-evidence\", \"title\": \"Assess the verification evidence\", \"anchor\": \"assess-the-verification-evidence\", \"start_line\": 70, \"end_line\": 107, \"content\": \"### Assess the verification evidence\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected candidate, accepted definitions, verification\\ncontracts (VER), and retained implementation evidence.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Retained evidence files:** A requirement-by-requirement assessment with\\n  actual check results and unresolved gaps at the specified evidence locations.\\n- **Formal artifacts:** No verification decision or lifecycle transition.\\n- **Transient working material:** Review notes not required as retained evidence.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Compare the candidate's observed behavior with each acceptance criterion.\\n2. Map every required check to its actual evidence file and pass condition.\\n3. Confirm that the evidence applies to the selected candidate and environment.\\n4. Run missing checks using the verification contract's (VER) commands or\\n   manual procedure. Retain their actual results.\\n5. Record each criterion as passed, failed, or not assessed, with its reason.\\n6. Retain material findings and their resolution with the verification evidence.\\n7. For a defect requiring implementation changes, identify a work order that\\n   covers the correction and is eligible for execution. Follow the recovery\\n   rules under \\u201cIf a procedure is blocked.\\u201d A completed work order does not\\n   become executable again because verification found a defect.\\n8. After the authorized correction, establish the new candidate identity and\\n   reassess the affected criteria against evidence for that candidate.\\n\\n**Harness command:** None for the substantive assessment. Use the check\\ncommands and manual assessments defined in the verification contracts (VER).\\nHarness validation alone does not prove the required behavior.\\n\\n**Completion:** Every required criterion has evidence or a visible gap.\\nFailures and missing checks are not reported as passes.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare the verification record](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#prepare-the-verification-record) binds the retained evidence to a verification record\\n(VREC). [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) uses it for the human's assessment.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"78a405625bfb24107f4b8f4f09ad84942d5710c55b27d58f3114da5f40688c3b\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-verification-decision\", \"title\": \"Record the verification decision\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-verification-decision\", \"start_line\": 255, \"end_line\": 300, \"content\": \"### Record the verification decision\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact human decision, ready verification record (VREC), and\\nunchanged candidate and evidence inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected verification record (VREC) receives\\n  its permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated record is retained through authorized Git\\n  actions. Historical candidate and evidence facts are preserved.\\n- **Transient working material:** The observed decision result and next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Recheck that the selected inputs still match the human decision.\\n2. Preview the exact transition.\\n3. Apply the same command when its gates pass and effects match the decision.\\n4. Inspect the verification record (VREC) and resulting workflow context.\\n5. Report its actual state, any blocker, and the evaluator's next action.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set VREC-ID=TARGET --decision VREC-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set VREC-ID=TARGET --decision VREC-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor supersession, select a successor verification record that is already\\n`verified` or `released` and preserves the old record\\u2019s work-order coverage.\\nUse the transition preview to assess that selection.\\n\\nFor `rejected`, add `--reason \\\"VREC-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to preview and apply.\\nFor `superseded`, add `--reason \\\"VREC-ID=SUCCESSOR-VREC-ID\\\"` to both. Preserve\\nthe old record; do not rewrite its candidate or evidence to match a new result.\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected verification record (VREC) has the recorded\\ndecision. Referenced work orders (WO) and release records (RLS) remain unchanged.\\n\\n**Later use:** For PR-based work, [Publish the verification decision](PULL_REQUEST.md#publish-the-verification-decision)\\nas the final commit under the existing grant. Eligible verified coverage\\nsupports the selected delivery path.\\nA rejection or supersession follows the evaluator's remediation or selection\\nprocedure; it does not authorize new implementation scope.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"99e090908551d2012bdadac654496a2c14eefe9399b04112fcf067f6386854d7\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-final40-20261012\\\\claude-361\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"892ec2fedefc272f6bc2580268395e487f392cf5d92a3ea81fac015761bc87a8\", \"bytes\": 8641, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"verification-coverage\", \"title\": \"Verification coverage\", \"anchor\": \"verification-coverage\", \"start_line\": 117, \"end_line\": 123, \"content\": \"## Verification coverage\\n\\nA verification record (VREC) MUST bind one or more\\nwork orders (WO), all their declared verification contracts (VER), retained\\nevidence, and one exact clean candidate commit. Preparing a verification\\nrecord (VREC) does not change its state to `verified`.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d0359e722c997b266376b6644404fca0db87d8718a79d2f2503aca0669936adf\"}]}]}",
  "is_error": false

Preparation performs no merge, publication,\\ndeployment, or release decision.\\n\\n**Later use:** A ready release record (RLS) proceeds to [Obtain the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#obtain-the-release-decision-when-required). \\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d3fcc6f4d9565acc0d714479b8b27df0173ce927ec4d36a757bf1f5710f34942\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"title\": \"Record the release decision, when required\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"start_line\": 117, \"end_line\": 159, \"content\": \"### Record the release decision, when required\\n\\n**Inputs:** The human's exact decision and unchanged release inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected release record (RLS) receives the\\n  permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated release record (RLS), retained through\\n  authorized Git actions.\\n- **Transient working material:** The applied result and current next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. A new operation key\n126\tstill has its own guarded command/receipt; retrying the original key has no new\n127\teffect. A refusal creates no accepted receipt.\n128\t\n129\tDomain reads select either an immutable baseline or an explicit context/version.\n130\tExact revision, work context, comparison, impact, verification lineage and check\n131\tall return selection identity, provenance, evaluator identity and completeness.\n132\tComparison explicitly names both views. Check is read-only and checkpoint-free;\n133\tit reports released findings and cannot apply a lifecycle transition. Operation\n134\tlookup returns the recorded receipt, not a recomputed result at the latest view.\n135\tUnsupported live-view forms are refused until their semantics are qualified.\n136\t\n137\tDomain and MCP reads share handlers. Context completeness requires all selected\n138\tgoverning artifacts and declared paths; truncated results cannot establish a\n139\tgoverning claim. The pinned reference fixture has 12 governing IDs and 11 paths\n140\tfor WO-RLS-038; VREC dependencies remain separately classified.\n141\t\n142\t## Validation at each stage\n143\t\n144\t| Stage | Required assessment | Meaning of success |\n145\t| --- | --- | --- |\n146\t| Decode | Strict UTF-8, unique JSON keys, integer-only request numbers, closed wire shape, contained source paths and configured source identity | A request can be evaluated; no authority or mutation follows from decoding |\n147\t| Import | Complete Git manifest, raw byte/provenance equality, released parsing and relation validation, all referenced targets resolved | A faithful historical baseline; imported lifecycle claims acquire no new decision event |\n148\t| Draft creation/revision | Released standalone draft classification, server rights, protected-field comparison and exact input selection | A saved draft may retain the evaluator's narrow permitted incompleteness; malformed content or supplied invalid relations refuse |\n149\t| Freeze | Complete selection, resolvable declared edges, canonical manifest and version guards | An immutable baseline of that selection; draft members remain drafts |\n150\t| Context/read/check | Explicit view, exact released context/findings, original-path historical resolver and honest resource limits | A bounded observation; `complete` does not mean approved or gate-passing |\n151\t| Approval/verification/release | Unsupported in this sandbox | No remote command can confer a human decision or produce a verified/released record |\n152\t\n153\tThe draft stage uses the selected public 0.22.1 evaluator. Its archive and payload\n154\tare fixed by SPEC-HAG-003. Earlier Phase 1 reports retain their original 0.22.0\n155\tobservations and unresolved-dependency status as historical evidence.\n156\t\n157\t## Read request and response details\n158\t\n159\t`server/contracts/read-v1.json` defines the seven POST request variants and their\n160\tresponse shapes. HTTP path operation/project and body values must agree. MCP\n161\tuses the same normalized request and authenticated handler. A context selector\n162\trequires its exact version. If that version has changed, refuse with 409; no\n163\timplicit latest view or historical context reconstruction is promised. Freeze a\n164\tselection when later reads need an immutable identity. A compare request names\n165\ttwo views in the same project.\n166\t\n167\t| Read | Selection and returned data |\n168\t| --- | --- |\n169\t| `revision` | Artifact ID and revision ID must match the selected view. Return the complete StoredRevision, including raw bytes; a known revision outside that view is an unknown selected identity |\n170\t| `work-context` | Selected work order, governing bindings, exact declared paths, dependencies and relevant decisions in separate fields; embed the unchanged checkpoint-free evaluator result |\n171\t| `compare` | Added/removed/changed artifact bindings plus added/removed resolved relation triples; a missing side of a binding is null |\n172\t| `impact` | The root and reverse reachability through known declared relations at the selected view, within depth; exclude the root from the returned artifact list |\n173\t| `lineage` | The root and connected declared verification/evidence relations, with endpoint revisions; this reports recorded links and claims, not new assurance |\n174\t| `check` | Only a WO, VREC, RLS or DEC accepted by the selected released checkpoint-free `check`; return its JSON unchanged with the selected binding |\n175\t| `cypher` | Columns and rows from the admitted query, bound to the selected view; column names and row widths agree and graph values expose only the documented public properties |\n176\t\n177\tSort domain bindings by artifact ID, paths lexically, and edges by\n178\t`(source.artifact_id, kind, target.artifact_id)`. Preserve evaluator output and\n179\tCypher row order. A read's `provenance` names the unique Git sources of its selected\n180\tinputs; synthetic draft-only examples may have none. Draft provenance is retained\n181\tin each revision envelope. Resolve every returned revision through the view.\n182\tFor comparison, resolve each side independently. These equality and resolution\n183\tchecks require the service; JSON Schema checks only their shapes.\n184\t\n185\t`complete=true` means that this response contains the whole requested answer at\n186\tthe stated view and no unresolved references. It can still contain draft hints,\n187\topen decisions, failed gates or a missing historical binding in the unchanged\n188\tevaluator result. When missing bindings prevent the requested assessment, report\n189\t`complete=false` with `binding_unavailable` and identify the exact missing input\n190\tin evaluator output. Do not convert `not_assessable` into a pass.\n191\t\n192\tBudgets apply to the aggregate graph rows across all returned collections, not\n193\t500 rows per nested array. Paths and unresolved-reference entries also consume\n194\tthat allowance. The byte budget includes the entire serialized response and\n195\tembedded evaluator output; never truncate that JSON. Traversal stops must be\n196\tvisible even if the last returned node has no displayed outgoing edge. A bounded\n197\tpartial response uses `complete=false`, the specific limit and concrete\n198\tinstructions to repeat at the same view with a narrower selection. That strategy\n199\tdoes not turn a partial work context into a governing claim. If the operation\n200\thas no meaningful narrower selection, repeat with a larger budget within the\n201\tfixed limits; if the minimum honest response cannot fit, refuse with 429.\n202\tUnresolved graph targets require a new complete view, not silent continuation at\n203\tan altered context version. No pagination cursor or server-side read session is\n204\tintroduced in this initial contract.\n205\t\n206\tThe baseline GET retrieves one canonical manifest resource, not a row query:\n207\t`{schema: \"se-harness-artifact-baseline/v1\", baseline_id, manifest}`. Validate the\n208\tmanifest with `BaselineManifest`, recompute its identity, and return the full\n209\tselection and resolved relations. The 2 MiB response limit still applies; reject\n210\tan import/freeze whose complete baseline response cannot fit before committing.\n211\tDo not clip the manifest to the graph-query row budget or label a fragment as B.\n212\tOperation GET returns exactly the stored accepted `remote-result/v1` object for\n213\tthe authenticated principal/project/key. Status GET reports project UUID, schema\n214\trevision, readiness, actual evaluator and component identities, and the supported\n215\tprotocols. Missing built/qualified identities keep readiness false. Neither GET\n216\trequires a context selector; operation lookup never guesses an acceptance.\n217\t\n218\t## Accepted receipts, refusals and retry order\n219\t\n220\t`server/contracts/result-v1.json` defines immutable accepted receipts and stable\n221\tremote refusal codes. Every successful mutation returns HTTP 200 and one UUIDv4\n222\t`receipt_id`. Store that entire result with the operation. Bind `request_digest`\n223\tto SHA-256 of `se-harness-remote-command/v1`, one LF, and canonical JSON of the\n224\tcomplete validated command. Canonicalize manifest entries as their declared set\n225\tbefore hashing; retain original document bytes and all expected versions. Reject\n226\tduplicate manifest entries before normalization. Credentials, connection metadata\n227\tand transport timestamps are outside the command and digest.\n228\t\n229\tAn accepted result's project `after` equals `before + 1`. For context open,\n230\tcontext `before` is null and `after` is zero. Create/revise increments the context\n231\tonce; freeze reports equal context versions. Import has a null context version\n232\trecord. The returned view names the imported/frozen baseline or resulting context;\n233\taffected revision IDs are sorted unique IDs created by this operation, so an\n234\tidentical-source reimport may report none. Receipt IDs are correlation identities,\n235\tnot substitutes for revision or baseline hashes.\n236\t`affected_artifacts` supplies the corresponding artifact/revision bindings, so\n237\tcreation with automatic ID allocation returns the allocated artifact ID directly.\n238\tIts revision set must equal `affected_revision_ids`; a refusal returns both empty.\n239\t\n240\tApply checks in this order:\n241\t\n242\t1. Authenticate and enforce project/operation access, then perform bounded strict\n243\t   decoding and shape checks. Reject unknown fields such as caller-supplied actor.\n244\t2. For a valid command, compute its request digest and inspect the accepted key.\n245\t   Equal digest returns the original result immediately, even after versions or\n246\t   the configured tuple change. Different digest returns key-reuse conflict.\n247\t   Current project access remains required; never evaluate a retry as a new write.\n248\t3. For a new key, check the supported tuple, known selections, then project,\n249\t   context and selected-revision guards in that order. Refuse the first mismatch.\n250\t4. Check source/protected input and invoke the released evaluator against the\n251\t   bound selection. Invalid draft/import, incomplete freeze and unavailable\n252\t   mandatory bindings have distinct 422 codes. Resource refusal is 429.\n253\t5. Recheck guards and selection in the write transaction, write all effects and\n254\t   receipt, then commit. On a concurrent equal-key conflict, read the winner's\n255\t   committed receipt. Never update a stale request's expectations automatically.\n256\t\n257\tMalformed input uses 400, unauthenticated 401, forbidden 403, unknown accessible\n258\tidentity 404, stale/key/source/tuple conflict 409, invalid content 422 and resource\n259\trefusal 429. The schema enumerates the `HAG_REMOTE_*` codes. These codes wrap the\n260\tremote operation; existing evaluator codes and JSON remain unchanged. Refusals\n261\thave no receipt and no affected revisions. Populate correlation/view/versions\n262\tonly when known and authorized; otherwise use null. When versions are returned\n263\ton refusal, before equals after. Read refusals use null command correlation and\n264\tversions. Denial must not leak another project's identities or findings.\n265\t\n266\tThe schemas describe the selected evaluator profile as well as wire shapes.\n267\tTheir pinned evaluator constants are compatibility checks: a well-formed but\n268\tdifferent version/archive/payload is 409, not malformed JSON. Keep those checks\n269\tseparate from primitive shape decoding and accepted-key recovery. Strictly\n270\tdecode base64 and require its canonical encoding before digest calculation;\n271\tinvalid base64 is malformed input, while invalid decoded TOML is invalid draft\n272\tcontent. A successful shape check alone never supplies an admission decision.\n273\t\n274\tA lost response, evaluator process crash or ambiguous database commit is not an\n275\taccepted or refused receipt. The client reports transport uncertainty and uses\n276\toperation lookup or an identical retry. A 404 lookup alone cannot prove that a\n277\tconcurrent transaction rolled back. A known precommit failure leaves no effects;\n278\tan unknown commit must be reconciled against the authoritative operation store.\n279\t\n280\t## Scenario and schema qualification\n281\t\n282\t`tests/hosted_artifact_graph/fixtures/scenarios-v1.json` maps all twelve\n283\tVER-HAG-001 cases to explicit positive/failure outcomes and storage support. Every\n284\thosted execution entry is `unperformed`. Its wire examples contain synthetic\n285\tidentities and demonstrate shape only; their apparent receipt values are not\n286\tobserved acceptances. The original fixed canonical vectors remain unchanged.\n287\t\n288\tFor independent shape qualification, install `jsonschema==4.26.0` in a disposable\n289\tenvironment and run its Python against:\n290\t\n291\t```text\n292\tpython -I -B tests/hosted_artifact_graph/validate_wire_contracts.py\n293\tpython -m unittest tests.test_hosted_artifact_graph\n294\t```\n295\t\n296\tThe first command registers the three local schemas without network resolution,\n297\tvalidates fixed vectors and the complete source manifest, and exercises accepted\n298\tand rejected shapes. It does not introduce a core runtime dependency. The second\n299\tcommand checks fixed bytes and digests through the existing test entry point.\n300\tNeither command executes service admission, transactions, Cypher or recovery.\n301\t\n302\t## Physical representation\n303\t\n304\tProject stores identity, schema revision and the integer command guard. Artifact\n305\tstores project-scoped identity. Revision stores its canonical `envelope_json`,\n306\t`document_base64`, artifact ID, raw document digest and derived type/status.\n307\tBaseline stores `manifest_json`; its SELECTS edges are derived from that manifest.\n308\tDraftContext stores base baseline, selected work order, version and proposals.\n309\tOperation stores project/principal/key, semantic request digest and immutable\n310\t`result_json`. JSON text properties retain exact machine structures without\n311\texpanding scalar fields into graph nodes.\n312\t\n313\tHAS_REVISION links Artifact to Revision. SELECTS links Baseline to Revision.\n314\tBASED_ON links DraftContext to Baseline. PROPOSES links DraftContext to Revision\n315\twith the selected artifact ID. DECLARES links Revision to the target Artifact,\n316\twith `kind` and `target_artifact_id`; resolve the target revision through the view.\n317\tCross-project edges, duplicate selections, and edges inconsistent with canonical\n318\tcontent fail import/export checks. Unresolved authoring placeholders remain\n319\texplicit findings and cannot become invented valid target nodes.\n320\t\n321\tThe public Cypher surface uses the selected project's Artifact and Revision\n322\tnodes, its selected Baseline (or context/base), and the corresponding storage\n323\tedges above. Project exposes only project ID, schema revision and the observed\n324\tcommand version. Artifact exposes project/artifact IDs. Revision exposes its IDs,\n325\ttype, status, document digest, envelope JSON and document base64. Baseline exposes\n326\tits IDs and manifest JSON. DraftContext exposes its IDs, selected work order,\n327\tbase baseline and context version. DECLARES exposes kind and target artifact ID;\n328\tPROPOSES exposes the selected artifact ID. Other edge properties are not public.\n329\t\n330\tOperation nodes and their result JSON are private to command handling and the\n331\tprincipal-scoped operation lookup. They are not available through Cypher. A\n332\tquery cannot use internal labels/properties, an unselected revision, another\n333\tbaseline/context, or caller-authored project filters to widen this surface. The\n334\tservice must apply that projection before query execution and use the same\n335\tread-only transaction snapshot for selection and results. This is application\n336\tadmission; it does not resolve RISK-HAG-001 or prove database privileges.\n337\t\n338\t`graph-v1.cypher` supplies six composite/single uniqueness keys, key/content\n339\texistence constraints and explicit lookup indexes. Memgraph requires separate\n340\tindexes for uniqueness constraints ([official constraint documentation](https://memgraph.com/docs/fundamentals/constraints)).\n341\tSchema creation must be an explicit operator step on an empty store; later\n342\tstartup verifies it and refuses mismatch.
